documents.s: Bought It... Yet Human Desire Is Truly Bottomless...

documents.t: At the end of last year, I finally decided to get a TV for the living room, because I really couldn't stand the whole family cramming into my study to watch movies together on a single 32" monitor... After thinking it over again and again, I bought this cheap 86" TV.

After using the TV's built-in Google TV for a while, I noticed that videos with external/separate subtitle files easily suffered from subtitle out-of-sync issues and the like. So the beast inside couldn't hold back anymore, and I bought what is currently hailed as the most powerful TV BOX — the Nvidia Shield TV Pro 2019. Yes, even though it's from 2019, it somehow still has the best performance on the market... Makes you wonder whether the hardware was overkill back then or other brands are just being stingy with specs...

Damn expensive — It actually cost over 6k NTD. Even the latest Google TV Streamer 4K (a 2024 product) only costs around 3k+ NTD, yet this five-plus-year-old piece of hardware still sells for this much... The SoC is genuinely fast — I looked up the Nvidia Tegra X1+ (the same chip as the Nintendo Switch... roughly 5th-gen i5 level performance). It's about twice as fast as the MediaTek chip in the Google Streamer 4K (though power draw is triple at 15W). 4K AI Upscaling — Actually, this feature was the main reason I bought it, and it's also its biggest selling point. However, in initial use my untrained eyes can't tell a huge difference yet... Plus not every app supports it (for example, Duboku doesn't trigger Upscaling), though maybe I just haven't configured it right—I'll try again soon. Gaming stream — Since I don't use Geforce Now, I can't comment on it, but I have used moonlight to stream my Steam games (Ace Combat 7). It looks pretty decent and pairs smoothly with a Bluetooth controller. The next step will probably be gradually turning it into part of an entertainment center without messing up Android (besides Emby which I already use, maybe streaming games via moonlight... or running something like an emulator collection).

Lately I've been stuck in a To be or Not to be state... It started because what I really want is a laptop with a dedicated GPU to run a Linux host (since right now, outside of the Steam Deck's desktop mode, I don't have a physical Linux terminal to use), and I'd really like to set up a penguin machine as a daily driver (a toy that can actually get work done). Considering that buying a brand-new laptop outright doesn't seem as cost-effective as building a new Gaming Server and freeing up the gaming laptop currently filling that role to repurpose it, I dove headfirst into researching desktop builds. Here's what makes it tough: Haven't followed desktop builds and specs in ages — Since 2011, I haven't bought any desktop that wasn't meant to be a server; I switched completely to laptops. My shopping habits also changed from going to Guanghua Digital Plaza to buy parts to browsing PChome, ordering online, and waiting for delivery at home... Going back to DIY feels really unfamiliar now, and I have no mental baseline left. Gap between budget and expectations — My mental model was still stuck in the era when laptops cost more than desktops. After looking around, I have to admit that the PMs behind every laptop spec actually worked hard to balance the configuration... Looking at desktops makes it way too easy to fall into the trap of "just spend a bit more for better specs," only to blow past the budget by the end—yet sticking to the budget leaves specs feeling slightly lacking and hard to swallow. After all that, it feels like only winning the lottery could solve it.... =_=!! It's gotten to the point where I'm thinking I might as well put that money into stocks instead... That'd probably give a better return... Besides, the moment I turn on my computer, two kids pull chairs up on my left and right, squeezing into my 120cm-wide desk and asking "Daddy, what are you doing..." It really kills any urge to buy one...

Notes Brave users need to turn off Brave Shields, otherwise the script will be blocked from running For those who want the filenames directly in Traditional Chinese, please click CC開啟 (Enable CC) first—it will convert the filenames to Traditional Chinese Downloading all together merges all volumes into a single file for download If there is a problem downloading any image, it will throw an Error instead of giving you an epub with missing images

documents.t: Chinese power-fantasy web novels are trickier—basically you have to find websites offering full-book txt downloads. Currently, I go to Free Novel Net (免費小說網) to download the full-book txt files. Because Chinese web novels easily run into millions of words and generally only contain text anyway, I don't expect covers or illustrations...

Since I always read on a kindle, I forcibly convert txt files to epub for archiving. Also, since I work in a Linux (penguin) environment most of the time now, the conversion tool naturally has to run on Linux. You ask why not use a web-based converter? Mainly because Chinese web novels have too much text, free online converters can't handle them, and I just want to stay a freeloader..

txt2epub github - There are many tools with the same name; I picked this one because it can be installed with yay, while most others are installed via pip. On Archlinux, I just run yay -S txt2epub and it's done... ~~Basic syntax [Kiwi]#> txt2epub -o </path/filename.epub> --author <author Name> --title <book title> --cover-image <filename.jpg> chapter01.txt chapter02.txt chapter03.txt Notes This thing is purely a CLI command. If you want a GUI, use pip to install another Python txt2epub—I saw a GUI version Make sure the text is unicode before converting, otherwise there will be issues

Before this, I used txt2epub for conversion, but found the text formatting of the converted files was a complete mess, so I switched to kaf-cli, which can also be installed directly with yay. The syntax is very similar to txt2epub. An excerpt of the instructions from GitHub is as follows: Command-line mode parameters Usage of kaf-cli: -align string 标题对齐方式: left、center、righ。环境变量KAF_CLI_ALIGN可修改默认值 (default "center") -author string 作者 (default "YSTYLE") -bookname string 书名: 默认为txt文件名 -bottom string 段落间距(单位可以为em、px) (default "1em") -cover string 封面图片可为: 本地图片, 和orly。 设置为orly时生成orly风格的封面, 需要连接网络。 (default "cover.png") -cover-orly-color string orly封面的主题色, 可以为1-16和hex格式的颜色代码, 不填时随机 -cover-orly-idx int orly封面的动物, 可以为0-41, 不填时随机, 具体图案可以查看: https://orly.nanmu.me (default -1) -filename string txt 文件名 -font string 嵌入字体, 之后epub的正文都将使用该字体 -format string 书籍格式: all、epub、mobi、azw3。环境变量KAF_CLI_FORMAT可修改默认值 (default "all") -indent uint 段落缩进字数 (default 2) -lang string 设置语言: en,de,fr,it,es,zh,ja,pt,ru,nl。环境变量KAF_CLI_LANG可修改默认值 (default "en") -line-height string 行高(用于设置行间距, 默认为1.5rem) -match string 匹配标题的正则表达式, 不写可以自动识别, 如果没生成章节就参考教程。例: -match 第.{1,8}章 表示第和章字之间可以有1-8个任意文字 -max uint 标题最大字数 (default 35) -out string 输出文件名，不需要包含格式后缀 -tips 添加本软件教程 (default true) -unknow-title string 未知章节默认名称 (default "章节正文") -volume-match string 卷匹配规则 (default "^第[0-9一二三四五六七八九十零〇百千两 ]+[卷部]") PS: 在darwin(mac、osx)上-tips参数要设置为false的方法 kaf-cli -filename 小说.txt -tips=0 Command-line mode instructions Convert 全职法师.txt and set the author name to 乱 # windows 10: win + s 搜索powershell cd d:/ d:/kaf-cli.exe -author 乱 -filename d:/全职法师.txt # linux / mac下, 把kaf-cli-linux/kaf-cli-darwin重命名为kaf-cli, 放到用户目录 # 把小说和kaf-cli放到用户目录下, 打开终端执行 cd ~ ./kaf-cli -author 乱 -filename ./全职法师.txt # 如果kaf-cli放到path里了, 或者在aur安装的可以执行: kaf-cli -author 乱 -filename ~/全职法师.txt # 命令行的简单模式（功能和拖拽模式一样） kaf-cli ~/全职法师.txt

Basically, for Japanese light novels, I just throw them into my light novel library — Calibre-Web — and use Calibre-Web's built-in feature to send books to my Kindle, so there's no problem there. However, I haven't set up a Calibre-Web instance for Chinese web novels yet (maybe later if the collection grows, or I'll put them into my general books Calibre library). Regardless of the future, right now if I want to manually push them to Kindle, I rely on Amazon's official send to kindle, which has a web-based uploader. Once it's done, you can download it on your Kindle and enjoy reading non-stop...

documents.s: Finally Ran Into It... Arch Linux Bricked...

documents.t: I used to see people say that if you use Arch Linux, you need to be mentally prepared for it to randomly die after an update. Having used it for nearly 10 years (Wait!! Am I really that old already? I started using it in 2015...), honestly, I had never once experienced a crash from an update, so I had a hard time understanding why anyone would refuse to update just to avoid breaking things.... Until last week, when I casually hit my remote desktop with a yay -Syu --noconfirm and then discovered... there was no "then". The machine looked powered on, yet remote connections failed. I went into ESXi to check the Console and it was a completely black screen.... It... bricked..

How would I know what the root cause is... I don't even know how to code.. However, I ran the following tests: Installed Manjaro with sddm + KDE plasma - Works normally Installed EndeavourOS with KDE - LiveDVD boots, but black screen after a fresh install Re-install Tried options like linux-6.14, linux-lts-6.12, etc., and it still booted to a black screen after installation and reboot Switched to gdm + KDE Plasma - Works, though inside ESXi only Wayland works normally And all of these issues also occurred when tested under VMWare Workstation 17 Pro....

sddm does not get along with VMware—aside from Manjaro, anything using sddm gives a black screen on boot X11 does not get along with gdm—even though using gdm shows a display, trying to log into a plasma-x11 session runs into issues Based on the two points above, Broadcom forgot to pray to the gods VMware has been disliked by everyone ever since its change of ownership...

My current setup is gdm+KDE Plasma, but because wayland-plasma doesn't support VNC and this machine is mainly used as my VDI, I used systemd to run vncserver@:1.service so the machine starts a plasma-x11 session over VNC on boot. So far it hasn't had any issues, though it looks like I'll eventually have to migrate from ESXi to PVE. On a side note, this incident didn't affect my other console-only Arch Linux machines, so strictly speaking it doesn't really count as Arch Linux bricking. Great!! My confidence in Arch Linux didn't drop—it actually went up (wait, what??)

Recently I got a bit diligent about updating my system... and then my UniFi Controller blew up right under a single yay -Syu --noconfirm.
documents.s: UniFi Controller Broke Again (and Again) Because of an AUR MongoDB Upgrade~~~

documents.t: After firing off yay -Syu --noconfirm and letting it run all the way through... the UniFi Controller Web UI became unreachable. Started investigating and found: systemctl status unifi.service reported active and ok, yet netstat -an showed no listening port for UniFi Controller. Checked /var/log/unifi/server.log and saw exit code=62. Checked systemctl status mongodb.service and saw exit code=62 there too; looking into it revealed MongoDB couldn't start normally because the database version was too old. Checked /var/log/mongodb/mongodb.log and confirmed the MongoDB data version was 7.0, while the updated mongodb-bin package in the AUR was version 8.2—too big of a version gap, so it refused to start. Switched to installing the mongodb80-bin package, which allowed upgrading MongoDB's major version to 8.0 via commands. The frustrating detour part: MongoDB's database upgrade concept: MongoDB cannot skip multiple versions in one jump when upgrading a database (yes, MongoDB's binary version and database version aren't automatically coupled—they're separate and must be upgraded manually). Going from 7.0 to 8.2 requires stepping 7.0 --> 8.0 --> 8.2. Generally a newer version is compatible with the previous version's database, whereas a newer database cannot work with an older binary. The chaotic detour experience: First I removed both the unifi and mongodb-bin packages, installed mongodb80-bin instead, and upgraded the admin database from 7.0 --> 8.0 --> 8.2. Then I removed mongodb80-bin again and reinstalled mongodb-bin and unifi. systemctl status mongodb.service looked fine, and systemctl status unifi.service looked fine too, yet UniFi Controller still wouldn't come up—checking /var/log/unifi/server.log still showed exit code=62. No matter how much I looked around, I still couldn't figure out how to upgrade UniFi's own MongoDB database (this is probably because this old guy hadn't put skill points into the right tree... so I looked completely clueless here). And so I got stuck with the main MongoDB admin database upgraded fine, while UniFi's MongoDB database couldn't be upgraded.... Finally I checked UniFi's PKGBUILD file and discovered... its dependency just requires any mongodb.... In the end, pairing mongodb80-bin + unifi worked because 8.0 is compatible with a 7.0 database, and it magically came right back to life.....

The two main things learned from this incident: MongoDB concepts and upgrades — I still need to look into how to upgrade MongoDB databases other than admin (honestly I couldn't even list the databases). I need to look into how to upgrade UniFi in the future without hitting landmines. I tried running it in Docker before, though I didn't stick with it due to networking issues—maybe it's time to dig that back up.

To fix the issue that had been bothering me for a long time with lidarr's API connecting to Musicbrainz, I made some adjustments to my automated free pirated media setup(automated multimedia collection setup).
The root cause was that Musicbrainz changed its API-related settings, causing lidarr to fail to retrieve metadata from Musicbrainz properly, which basically rendered lidarr useless.

Simply put, the ultimate solution was to wait. Once you waited long enough, the lidarr dev team actually released an updated version of lidarr to work with Musicbrainz's new settings (though the text search part is still beyond saving). BUT since everyone couldn't wait earlier, before the dev team fixed it, people started using modified builds or adding mods. As a result, those who used a modified build found that upgrading directly to the new official version didn't work either—which led to the painful ordeal that followed.

Because this old guy proactively adopted the best solution available at the time(couldn't wait six or seven months and got itchy fingers), after the update I had no choice but to completely wipe the entire lidarr config, then reconfigure everything and re-import the files... Yeah... that process really was long and exhausting...

The biggest difference is that the fixed lidarr still cannot use text search like before to search directly by artist name or album name and add new. Instead, you have to go to Musicbrainz first to look up the artist's Artist ID or the album's Release group ID. Then go into lidarr's add new and use: lidarr:<artist ID/Release group ID> And just like before, select the cover that pops up and add it into lidarr.
Nothing special really—just that the author of the ChineseSubtitle plugin I used previously got too busy and abandoned the project...
After looking around, I switched to Bazarr. The setup was just as simple—just spin it up with Docker.

Bazarr is basically part of the *arr family too, so it integrates very well with the rest of my multimedia stack. However, with subtitles, it's like: if you can find them, you find them; if you can't, you can't—just like "whoever gets more votes wins, whoever gets fewer votes loses," a truism that's still basically stating the obvious...

Originally, based on reference guides, I wrapped the entire automedia stack (including radarr, sonarr, lidarr, jackett...) inside Gluten. However, Gluten's VPN has been acting up lately (honestly, I'm not even sure how long it's been broken). First I noticed jackett + flaresolverr were acting weird, so I moved that pair out of Gluten. Then while fixing lidarr (yep, the one mentioned above...), I found that add new search couldn't connect... After decisively moving lidarr out of Gluten, it worked immediately... So I moved everything in the entire automedia stack out of Gluten except qbittorrent. After all, that matches my ideal setup anyway—only qbittorrent goes through the VPN to stay safe, while the other services don't waste VPN bandwidth... And then I realized the issue mentioned in the reference guides—that they wouldn't be able to talk to each other if not placed together—had disappeared... (probably because I deliberately assigned static IPs to every container in automedia...)
Just add PUBLICIP_ENABLED=false under enviroment in docker-compose.yml and it's fixed.

documents.s: Long Time No Update, Missed You All

documents.t: Even though nobody really cares about what a middle-aged guy has been up to, I still want to jot things down like a diary—organizing what I've been doing lately and what I plan to do next.

To cut to the chase: it failed. Not only did I fail to build anything useful, I even paid for a full year of Gemini AI Pro. Still, there are a few takeaways I want to leave behind. Simply put, the failure of this vibe coding experiment can't be blamed entirely on Google. Even though plenty of people online say Gemini is trash at coding, blah blah blah, objectively speaking, the main reasons for the failure came down to two things: Not having a clear idea of what I actually wanted to build Strictly speaking, it's because I lack creativity. I came up with a bunch of ideas that seemed promising, only to realize in the end that the return wasn't worth the effort, there wasn't a real need, or someone had already written a great open-source project I could just use directly. That killed my motivation to keep burning brain cells on it. Knowing too little about programming concepts—even when AI wrote a mountain of code, I couldn't read it or tell where problems might arise This issue was glaringly obvious. From structuring a program's framework, planning architecture, choosing a language, and defining variables, to keeping the AI from going off the rails across multiple turns and designing for future maintenance and revisions from the start—all of that was far beyond my ability to plan ahead. In other words, no matter how good AI is at writing code, if the human drafting the blueprint has an empty head, it's still useless (okay, this applies to plenty of other domains too, like governing a country, a company, or a project). So for now, that whole effort is completely on hold. That said, strictly speaking, if I just ask AI to write simple shell scripts—things I can actually understand—it's still super handy.

Thought I was going to spill something here?? Nope. I'm not dumb enough to leak work details in a place like this. Just making a note for myself: emotionally, this period at work left me with some pretty unpleasant memories, so I'm leaving a footnote.

Strictly speaking, this is about the company issuing me a new laptop. This machine is pretty interesting: a Lenovo ThinkPad P16 Gen 3 with an NVIDIA RTX PRO 1000 GPU and two SSDs. I took advantage of a loophole during the company's Windows installation—one of the SSDs wasn't mounted, formatted, or brought under management—and installed Arch Linux on it for my writing setup. Now I can have a working Arch Linux environment even at the office without relying solely on WSL all the time (though my work Windows still has WSL too). As for the story of this Arch Linux setup, I might write more about it later if I feel like it—or just skip it if I don't.
Basically, I picked up a retired company Dell Latitude 5411 on the cheap and brought it home. After thinking about it for a while, I decided to turn it into my very first personal Arch Linux laptop.
Everything above was just trivial stuff over the past few months. What I've really been thinking about and working on lately is the following.

For a long time now, I've wanted to completely overhaul my home gaming setup. Ideally, I'd have a machine in the living room capable of streaming or running games up to a certain performance tier natively, while heavy-hitting PC AAA titles could either be played directly in the study or streamed out to the living room. So I took inventory of all the machines I already have (all old hardware) and started planning the revamp. NVIDIA SHIELD TV Pro​ This is currently the main set-top box for watching videos in my living room. I once tried installing RetroArch and Moonlight on it, and here's what I found: Moonlight runs, but it depends heavily on a gaming streaming machine running Sunshine. RetroArch runs smoothly up through the SNES (SFC) era, though storage space is a major issue. Steam Deck​ As my main handheld, I've actually been thinking about switching it to another Steam account, setting up emulators properly, and moving the whole thing along with its dock into the living room to replace our current Switch (since the Switch Joy-Cons are broken... and the screen has cracks too). However, this approach hits a couple of roadblocks: The Steam Deck's emulation capability starts struggling past the PS2 era—though it really is my best living-room console option right now. It's my personal toy, and I really don't want the kids wrecking it. Dell Latitude 5411​ This machine has zero value for gaming because it has no discrete GPU and only 8GB of RAM—it contributes nothing meaningful to gaming. However, because it exists, it took over the Steam Deck's role as my casual Linux desktop. That's the only reason I can free up the Steam Deck in the first place. MSI GL73​ This gaming laptop equipped with an NVIDIA RTX 2060 Mobile is currently my best-performing gaming machine, running Windows—the most game-friendly OS.

The vision sounds great, but reality is brutally harsh—I ran into problems before even starting the work. The biggest issue is that this home entertainment center isn't meant for just me alone. Almost all existing tools and approaches assume one big premise: Owner of the games = Player = Controller of everything The moment you have to factor in kids playing too—controlling their playtime and restricting which games they can play—you immediately land on the solution of adding a Steam child account into a Family Group so you can manage kids' playtime and game libraries via Steam's built-in features. As for emulators, since storage on a living-room device is limited, you simply put only curated games on it from the start. That sounds lovely, right? But here's the problem: if the living-room machine is powerful enough on its own and doesn't need streaming, everything is solved—it's just a standalone console. What if you need a beefier streaming host to run games that demand high-end hardware? Long story short, I tested running games on the Steam Deck via Steam Link over my home network, and "utterly unplayable" doesn't even begin to describe it... Meanwhile, the Moonlight/Sunshine approach has no account isolation whatsoever (since it streams the entire desktop). So if I want to include AAA titles, I'd have to dedicate a streaming host for them, and on top of that figure out how to stream the games I want to play, how to separate accounts and isolate sessions... Things get way too complicated, and I'd need to add more machines to pull it off. Implementation Progress So Far​ Right now, I've been unifying my bare-metal Arch Linux setups and aligning their configurations closely with the Steam Deck's SteamOS + EmuDeck integration—organizing my previously neglected emulator resources while also paving the way to eventually stop using Windows altogether...

If I give up on living-room streaming, I could repurpose the Steam Deck into an emulation box plus some kid-friendly / living-room-friendly Steam games. The only catch is I'd effectively lose my handheld, or have to share the console with the kids... Until I buy a new gaming rig, this isn't a bad compromise—assuming the kids' mom doesn't make me kneel on a washboard and dismantle the whole thing for making it too convenient for the kids to play games...

When configuring Duo / Sunshine for multi-user concurrent streaming or family multi-account sharing, the most stable storage logic is "Centralized read-only sharing for ROMs and BIOS, local isolation for game saves per account": Read-Only Centralized Sharing (NAS / RomM): ROMs and BIOS are stored on the NAS and mapped to each device via SMB (e.g., Z:\roms and Z:\bios). Local Multi-Account Save Isolation (Saves / States): User game saves (.srm, .sav) and Save States must strictly avoid writing back to network shared directories. If saves are shared, simultaneous or multi-player gameplay of the same title will cause file lock contention and progression overwrite disasters.
documents.s: I. Architecture Planning: Centralized Read-Only Library and Multi-User Local Save Isolation

documents.t: The remote NAS shared directory must follow a standard hierarchical structure: \\<NAS_IP>\Emulation\ <-- Network drive root directory (mapped as Z:\) ├── bios\ <-- BIOS for various systems (e.g., scph1001.bin, etc.) │ └── ... └── roms\ <-- Platform folder names must exactly match EmuDeck specifications ├── gba\ ├── ps2\ └── snes\

Open "File Explorer" ➔ "Map network drive". Select Z: for the drive letter, and enter \\<NAS_IP>\Emulation for the folder path (check "Reconnect at sign-in"). If Z: frequently disconnects with a cross mark upon booting due to network latency, a startup batch script can be created: @echo off timeout /t 5 /nobreak >nul net use Z: \\<NAS_IP>\Emulation /persistent:yes
documents.s: 2. Windows Local Startup Persistent Network Drive (Z:)

documents.t: During the "Prerequisites" stage of the EmuDeck for Windows installation wizard, even if no Android emulators are selected, it still forcefully downloads platform-tools (i.e., adb.zip) for extraction. When the installation target points directly to a network drive (Z:), SMB file handle locking latency or asynchronous write characteristics cause the script to misjudge file status during deletion or retry loops, leading to infinite waiting or application deadlock.
documents.s: 1. Causes of Installation Freezing on "adb.zip" When Pointing to a Network Drive

documents.t: Option A: Local Installation Followed by Directory Junction (Updated 2026-11-27: mklink /D creates a Directory Symbolic Link, which is compatible with network drives Z:\; mklink /J Junctions only support local drives) Bridging to NetDrive (Recommended, Most Robust)​ To completely avoid SMB permission privilege invocation issues running setup wizards over remote paths, complete the installation locally first and then establish symbolic links: Force Terminate Residual Processes: Open PowerShell as Administrator and terminate background locking processes: Stop-Process -Name "adb" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Stop-Process -Name "EmuDeck*" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Manually Create Dummy Files to Prevent Check Interruption: $paths = @( "$env:USERPROFILE\EmuDeck", "$env:APPDATA\EmuDeck", "$env:TEMP" ) foreach ($p in $paths) { if (Test-Path $p) { New-Item -ItemType File -Path "$p\adb.zip" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } } Execute Local Installation: Run the EmuDeck installer and select Custom Mode. Select a local drive for the target directory (such as the default C:\Users\%USERNAME%\Emulation). Uncheck all Android-related emulators in the emulator list. Create Directory Symbolic Links: Completely close EmuDeck after installation finishes, and delete the locally generated empty folders: Delete C:\Users\%USERNAME%\Emulation\roms Delete C:\Users\%USERNAME%\Emulation\bios Open CMD as Administrator to create directory symbolic links: mklink /D "C:\Users\%USERNAME%\Emulation\roms" "Z:\roms" mklink /D "C:\Users\%USERNAME%\Emulation\bios" "Z:\bios" Verification method: Open C:\Users\%USERNAME%\Emulation\roms and verify that files from Z:\roms can be read and operated normally. Option B: Manually Modify settings.json to Bypass ADB Check (Direct Installation to Z:)​ If you insist on pointing EmuDeck's installation root directory directly to Z:\, you can manually modify the configuration file to forcefully declare that ADB and Android modules have already been installed, causing the installation wizard to skip downloading, extracting, and deleting adb.zip: Force Terminate Installation Process: Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager, and forcefully terminate all EmuDeck, PowerShell, cmd.exe, and adb.exe processes. Modify settings.json to Declare Status: Open %USERPROFILE%\EmuDeck\settings.json (or %APPDATA%\EmuDeck\settings.json if in AppData) and manually set the status of adb and android to true and skip: { "tools": { "adb": { "installed": true, "configured": true }, "platformTools": { "installed": true } }, "android": { "installed": true, "configured": true, "skip": true } } Populate Local Dummy Tool Files and Clear Caches: Run the following commands in PowerShell to create dummy files passing existence checks and remove any stuck archive remnants: # Create platform-tools placeholder directory and dummy executable $toolsPath = "$env:USERPROFILE\EmuDeck\tools\platform-tools" New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $toolsPath -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue New-Item -ItemType File -Path "$toolsPath\adb.exe" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue # Clear lingering adb.zip in temporary directories Remove-Item "$env:USERPROFILE\EmuDeck\adb.zip" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Remove-Item "$env:TEMP\adb.zip" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Restart Installation: Right-click the EmuDeck installer and select "Run as administrator". The wizard will skip the ADB stage and proceed directly to the emulator selection and configuration page.
By default, EmuDeck points saves to the home directory saves folder (e.g., Z:\Emulation\saves). You must forcefully redirect save paths back to each user's local space:
documents.s: III. Multi-User Independent Save Configuration (Preventing Multi-User Progress Conflicts)

documents.t: Open RetroArch ➔ Go to "Settings" ➔ "Directory": Savefile Directory: Set to local path, e.g., C:\Users\%USERNAME%\EmuDeck\saves\ Savestate Directory: Set to local path, e.g., C:\Users\%USERNAME%\EmuDeck\states\ Enable "Save Saves to Current Directory" or "Sort Saves into Folders by Core Name" to ensure individual game saves are isolated.
documents.s: 1. RetroArch Save and Savestate Path Redirection

documents.t: PCSX2: Go to Settings ➔ Memory Cards, and ensure memory card files are located locally under %APPDATA%\PCSX2\memcards\ or C:\Users\%USERNAME%\Documents\PCSX2\memcards/. Strictly avoid pointing them to Z:\. Dolphin: GC/Wii virtual memory cards are created locally under %USERPROFILE%\Documents\Dolphin Emulator\ by default; maintaining the default local path is recommended.

If backing up personal local saves to a remote NAS is required, each account can create an independent scheduled script: robocopy "C:\Users\%USERNAME%\EmuDeck\saves" "\\<NAS_IP>\Backup\%USERNAME%_Saves" /MIR
documents.s: 3. Multi-User Automated Personal Save Backup (Scheduled Batch Task)

documents.t: For Arch Linux, it is recommended to use the official installation script combined with the Flatpak container architecture. 1. Install Prerequisite Dependencies​ sudo pacman -Syu --needed base-devel git curl flatpak zenity flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists flathub https://dl.flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo 2. Download and Run EmuDeck​ mkdir -p ~/Downloads/EmuDeck && cd ~/Downloads/EmuDeck curl -L -O https://www.emudeck.com/EmuDeck.desktop chmod +x EmuDeck.desktop ./EmuDeck.desktop In the installation wizard, choose Expert Mode. Storage directories can be set to local /home/<user>/Emulation, or pointed to a remote NFS/SMB directory pre-mounted via /etc/fstab: <NAS_IP>:/mnt/share/Emulation /mnt/Emulation nfs _netdev,nofail,x-systemd.automount 0 0

SteamOS (Steam Deck): Switch to Desktop Mode, download EmuDeck.desktop from the official website to the desktop and execute it, selecting installation to the SD card or internal storage. The system will automatically configure TDP and refresh rate optimization scripts. Ubuntu / Debian Derivatives: sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y flatpak git curl zenity dialog libfuse2 flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists flathub https://dl.flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dragoonDorise/EmuDeck/main/install.sh)" Fedora: sudo dnf install -y flatpak git curl zenity flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists flathub https://dl.flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dragoonDorise/EmuDeck/main/install.sh)"

Close Steam Before Execution: Completely exit the Steam client before generating shortcuts or saving box art to prevent write conflicts resulting in cache corruption. Verify Parsers Paths: Ensure that each platform's ROMs Directory correctly points to Z:\roms\<Platform_Name> or local symbolic link directories (e.g., C:\Users\%USERNAME%\Emulation\roms\<Platform_Name>). Parse & Save: Click Preview ➔ Parse to download covers and box art, review them, and click Save to Steam to write shortcuts.
documents.s: V. Steam ROM Manager (SRM) Injection and Notes

documents.s: BattleTech Mod Modification Overview and Implementation Workflow

documents.t: BattleTech's equipment and weapon system is entirely driven by JSON files. Every weapon, ammo bin, piece of equipment, and even projectiles themselves have independent JSON definition files. The core principles of modification lie in ensuring ID uniqueness and correct logical relationships.

Essential Tools: Use Notepad++ or other plain text editors to process JSON files, ensuring correct formatting without garbled characters. Copy and Naming: Directly copy factory files (e.g., Weapon_Autocannon_UAC20.json) to modify. Filenames must never duplicate, and it is recommended to add a custom suffix (e.g., _VerK). ID Consistency: The "Id" parameter inside the JSON file must exactly match the modified new filename, otherwise reading errors will occur when the game launches. Updated 2026-11-27 If you copy and create a new custom filename (rather than directly overwriting original files), the vanilla BattleTech engine will not automatically scan unregistered new JSON files. In practice, you must pair it with ModTek (writing a mod.json manifest in a custom Mod folder) or register new entries in VersionManifest.csv for the game to correctly load the equipment.

Store Generation Method (Conventional): Modify "Cost", "Rarity" (recommended to set lower for easier testing), and "Purchasable" (set to true) in Description, and remove the "BLACKLISTED" tag from "ComponentTags" so the equipment can randomly spawn in in-game galactic stores. Save Editor Method (Quick Testing): Utilize community-provided BattleTech Save Editor to directly write the newly created equipment ID into existing save inventories, launching the game to immediately install and test.
documents.s: 2. Methods for Implementing into the Game

documents.t: tip Ammunition is also worth modifying; at the very least, ammo quantity is crucial. In BattleTech's underlying architecture, the ammunition system adopts a rigorous "three-layer" mapping logic. To successfully fire a single bullet, you must ensure that the JSON configurations of the Weapon, AmmunitionBox, and Ammunition are perfectly linked together.
documents.s: BattleTech Ammo System Architecture and Custom Ammo Box JSON Modification Guide

documents.t: When a Mech attempts to fire in combat, the system sequentially executes the following checks: Layer 1 [Weapon End]: Reads the AmmoCategory parameter in the Weapon JSON (e.g., "AC20"), confirming what caliber of bullet the weapon consumes. Layer 2 [Mech Inventory]: Scans all equipment on the Mech, looking for physical ammo boxes where ComponentType is AmmunitionBox, and verifies whether the box can provide ammo of the "AC20" category. Layer 3 [Bullet Definition]: The AmmoID inside the ammo box points to an independent Ammunition JSON file (e.g., Ammunition_AC20.json). This underlying file truly defines the attributes of this bullet (such as armor-piercing or incendiary effects). 💡 Safe Modding Rule If your sole purpose is to "expand ammunition capacity", only modify the Capacity parameter of the AmmunitionBox, while keeping AmmoID pointing to the factory-default bullet file. This ensures the system will never encounter loading errors.
documents.s: 1. Ammo Pairing and Trigger Logic (System Logic)

documents.t: The ammo box is the "physical equipment" that players actually install onto Mechs in the refitting interface. Parameter Name (Key) Setting Impact & Description AmmoID Core Link Point: Specifies the bullet type contained in this ammo box. Must exactly match the underlying Ammunition file name (e.g., "Ammunition_AC20"). Must not be entered incorrectly, otherwise the weapon will show no ammunition. Capacity Ammunition Capacity: Total firing times provided by this ammo box. For example, setting it to 100 means this box allows a weapon consuming 1 ammo per shot to fire 100 times. ComponentType Main Component Classification: Must be set to "AmmunitionBox". Tells the system to judge it as an ammo container rather than a weapon or heat sink. ComponentSubType Sub-Component Classification: Must be set to "Ammunition". InventorySize Slots Occupied: Space occupied in a Mech location (such as legs, torso). Factory ammo typically occupies 1 slot. Tonnage Equipment Weight (Tons): Consumes part of the Mech's total weight allowance. Factory ammo is typically 1 ton. Description.Id Object ID: Must be exactly identical to the JSON file name of this ammo box.

If you want to create special bullets (e.g., high-explosive incendiary rounds that increase heat upon hit, or depleted uranium armor-piercing rounds with higher damage), you need to create a brand-new Ammunition JSON file and point the ammo box's AmmoID to it. File Example: You can copy the factory Ammunition_AC20.json to modify. Parameter Name (Key) Setting Impact & Description AmmoCategory Ammunition Caliber Category: Must match the weapon's AmmoCategory (e.g., "AC20"). Tells the system who this bullet is for. WeaponEffectID Exclusive Visual Effects: Optional. If this is a special bullet, you can specify different firing visual effects or tracer colors. HeatGeneratedModifier Heat Generation Modifier: Alters heat generated when firing this ammo. For example, 1.2 means weapon heat increases by 20% when firing this ammo. ArmorDamageModifier Armor Damage Modifier: Alters destructive power against armor. For example, 1.5 means 1.5x extra damage dealt to enemy armor. ISDamageModifier Internal Structure Damage Modifier: Alters destructive power against unarmored parts (Internal Structure). For example, 2.0 means extremely easy to destroy internal Mech components. InstabilityModifier Instability Modifier: Alters the multiplier for reducing target stability upon hit.

Below is a modified high-capacity (100 rounds) ammo box configuration template, which can be saved directly as Ammo_AmmunitionBox_UAC20_VerK.json: { "AmmoID" : "Ammunition_AC20", "Capacity" : 100, "Description" : { "Cost" : 150000, "Rarity" : 0, "Purchasable" : true, "Manufacturer" : "Kiwi Tech", "Model" : "High-Density Drum", "UIName" : "Ammo AC/20 Ver.K", "Id" : "Ammo_AmmunitionBox_UAC20_VerK", "Name" : "Ammo AC/20 Ver.K", "Details" : "A special AC/20 ammo drum adopting high-density compression technology, holding up to 100 rounds of standard AC/20 armor-piercing ammunition in a single slot.", "Icon" : "uixSvgIcon_equipment_AmmoBox" }, "BonusValueA" : "+ 100 Rounds", "BonusValueB" : "", "ComponentType" : "AmmunitionBox", "ComponentSubType" : "Ammunition", "PrefabIdentifier" : "", "InventorySize" : 1, "Tonnage" : 1, "AllowedLocations" : "All", "DisallowedLocations" : "All", "CriticalComponent" : false, "statusEffects" : [ ], "ComponentTags" : { "items" : [ "component_type_variant", "component_type_variant2" ], "tagSetSourceFile" : "" } }

tip In BattleTech, statusEffects is a very deep system. It can handle both "passive equipment bonuses (Passive)" and "negative effects triggered on hit (OnHit)". Every status effect consists of four main JSON blocks.
documents.s: BattleTech Status Effects and Buff Configuration

documents.t: These two blocks determine "how long the effect lasts" and "who it applies to". Parameter Name (Key) Settings Impact and Description durationData.duration Duration in turns: Set to -1 for permanent effect (as long as the equipment remains equipped). If set to a positive integer (like 2), it means the effect lasts for 2 turns (usually used for debuffs applied when hitting enemies). targetingData.effectTriggerType Trigger timing: • Passive: Passive constant, active as long as equipped. • OnHit: Triggered when weapon hits the target. targetingData.effectTargetType Target: • Creator: Applies to the mech equipping this weapon/component itself (Buff). • Target: Applies to the enemy mech hit by this weapon (Debuff). targetingData.showInStatusPanel UI display: true or false. Whether to show the icon of this buff/debuff in the combat screen status bar. Hidden passive abilities are usually set to false to avoid interface clutter.

Controls information displayed when this effect is clicked in the game interface. Parameter Name (Key) Settings Impact and Description Description.Id Unique effect identifier: Must be unique across the game. Strongly recommended to use the format StatusEffect-EquipmentName-EffectName. Description.Name Effect Name: Buff/Debuff name displayed on the UI. Description.Details Detailed Description: Text description for the effect on the UI. Description.Icon Interface Icon: Name of the SVG vector icon invoked (e.g., uixSvgIcon_equipment_TTS).

This is the most critical block, responsible for executing underlying numerical additions, subtractions, multiplications, and divisions. Parameter Name (Key) Settings Impact and Description statisticData.targetCollection Scope: • Weapon: Effect is limited to the weapon providing this buff itself. • StatCollection: Effect extends to all components and base stats of the entire mech. statisticData.statName Target property: Which system statistic you want to modify (refer to the "Common Property Name Dictionary" below). statisticData.operation Operation logic: • Float_Add / Int_Add: Addition operation (input negative numbers for subtraction). • Float_Multiply: Multiplication operation, used for multipliers (e.g., 1.1 means a 10% increase). statisticData.modValue Modification value: Specific number to change. Note: Must be wrapped in double quotes as a string in JSON (e.g., "-1.0" or "15"). statisticData.modType Data type: • System.Single: Corresponds to float (numbers with decimals). • System.Int32: Corresponds to integer (numbers without decimals).
When building special equipment, fill the following strings into statisticData.statName to modify corresponding mech or weapon capabilities.

Applicable when targetCollection is set to "Weapon", affecting only that specific weapon. Property Name (statName) Operation Recommendation Actual Effect Description AccuracyModifier Float_Add Accuracy modifier. Input negative values (like -1.0) to increase accuracy and lower shooting difficulty. DamagePerShot Float_Add Damage per shot increase. Directly increases the base damage of each bullet or laser. HeatGenerated Float_Add Heat generation modifier. Input negative values (like -5.0) to reduce heat generated when the weapon fires. EvasivePipsIgnored Int_Add Evasive pips ignored. Improves weapon's ability to ignore enemy Evasion points (e.g., 1 means ignoring 1 additional grid). MaxRange Float_Add Max range extension. Directly increases the maximum firing distance of the weapon.

Applicable when targetCollection is set to "StatCollection", affecting the entire mech's physique and movement. Property Name (statName) Operation Recommendation Actual Effect Description MaxHeat Int_Add Overheat threshold cap. Increases the total slot quantity of heat the mech can tolerate. HeatSinkCapacity Int_Add Base heat dissipation capacity. Extra heat dissipated at the end of each turn (similar to built-in heat sinks). WalkSpeed Float_Add Walking distance. Increases the single movement range of the mech on the combat map. RunSpeed Float_Add Sprint distance. Increases the maximum movement range of the mech when performing a Sprint. JumpDistanceMultiplier Float_Multiply Jump distance multiplier. Only effective if equipped with Jump Jets, increasing the limit of jump distance. DamageReductionMultiplierAll Float_Multiply Global damage reduction multiplier. E.g., 0.9 means damage from any source is reduced by 10% (extremely powerful defensive attribute). SensorSignatureModifier Float_Add Radar signature modifier. Input negative values (like -0.2) to make it harder for enemies to lock onto and discover this mech at a distance (stealth effect).

documents.t: info This article was automatically translated by Google "Gemini". The author does not guarantee its accuracy or wording. tip This article compiles the definitions and actual impacts of various parameters in PC game BattleTech weapon and equipment JSON files, categorized into four main groups.
documents.s: BattleTech Weapons & Equipment JSON Parameter Parsing

documents.t: Controls the weapon's hardware classification, range, and operational basis. Parameter Name (Key) Setting Impact & Description Category Major weapon category: e.g., Ballistic, Energy, Missile. Determines the Mech hardpoints applicable to the weapon. Type Weapon type: e.g., Autocannon, Laser, used for internal system logic identification. WeaponSubType Weapon sub-type: e.g., UAC20, further subdividing types, affecting ammo bin matching and pilot skill bonuses. RangeSplit Range thresholds: Formatted as [Short, Medium, Long]. Defines hit rate reduction determination points across different distance intervals. AmmoCategory Ammo category: e.g., AC20. The Mech must have the corresponding category of ammunition box installed to fire. HeatGenerated Heat generated per firing: Increases the Mech's heat level each time it fires.

Defines destructive power and supplemental combat effects caused when weapons fire. Parameter Name (Key) Setting Impact & Description Damage Base damage per single shot: Armor or internal structure value deducted when each ammunition round/beam hits. ShotsWhenFired Shots fired: Number of shots fired in a single attack command. Total damage = Base damage × Shots fired (if ProjectilesPerShot > 1, total damage is Damage × ShotsWhenFired × ProjectilesPerShot). ProjectilesPerShot Projectiles per shot: For scatter weapons (LBX) or missiles, how many independently calculated hitting projectiles a single ammo round splits into. Instability Stability damage: Deducts target stability upon hit. Accumulating enough leads to enemy Mech knockdown. AccuracyModifier Accuracy modifier: Negative values represent increased accuracy, positive values represent decreased accuracy. AttackRecoil Attack recoil: Hit penalty generated from continuous-round firing (UAC category is usually set higher). IndirectFireCapable Indirect fire capability: Boolean (true/false). Whether it can attack across obstacles ignoring Line of Sight (LoS).

Defines space occupancy and installation restrictions in the refit screen. Parameter Name (Key) Setting Impact & Description InventorySize Critical Slots: The amount of space occupied when installed in a Mech body part. Tonnage Equipment weight (tons): Occupies quota of the Mech's total weight capacity. AllowedLocations Allowed mounting locations: All means installable on the entire machine; can also restrict to e.g., MechHead.

Parameter Name (Key) Setting Impact & Description Description.Id Most core parameter. Must match the JSON filename exactly. BonusValueA / B Special effect hint: Green bonus text (e.g., + 50 Dmg.). Note: This is strictly a UI string; actual effects must be modified in Damage or statusEffects. ComponentTags Component tags: Affects store generation. Tagging BLACKLISTED prevents it from appearing in stores or salvage.

tip After modifying appearances, the pet's upgrade mechanism is still recognized by the system as a Pet and will not have independent experience points. It is recommended to use the Bag of Tricks mod to assist with experience and leveling management.
documents.s: Pathfinder: Kingmaker Save Editing Companion (Pet) Appearance and Model Guide

documents.t: Be sure to back up your original saves before making any modifications. Save Path: C:\Users\{Username}\AppData\LocalLow\Owlcat Games\Pathfinder Kingmaker\Saved Games (Note: AppData is a hidden system folder. You need to enable "Show hidden items" in File Explorer or type the path directly into the address bar.) File Format: The .zks save files are actually standard ZIP archives. Extract them directly using any decompression software. Recommended Editing Tool: Notepad++ with the JSTool Plugin is strongly recommended. Opening the JSON file and using JSTool's JSFormat feature automatically aligns the compacted JSON content into an easily readable tree structure.

After extracting the .zks archive, you will see many files. The two core files for modifying appearance are: File Name Content Description party.json Primary modification target. Records detailed information for "all characters" in the party (including the protagonist, NPC teammates, and pet companions). Changing companion races and appearances is done here. player.json Primarily records progress and personal status messages for the protagonist.

In party.json, all settings for each character are packaged within a large block (section) called "Descriptor". Here are the core parameters controlling appearance and identity: Parameter Name (Key) Setting Impact & Description "CustomName" Character Name. The best anchor point for locating a specific character (e.g., search for "Kiwi Von Hohenzollen" to find the character you want to modify). "CustomGender" Gender. Usually set to "Male" or "Female". "LeftHandedOverride" Left-handed setting. Boolean (true / false). "m_CustomPortrait" Custom Portrait. Specifies the 2D portrait folder ID used by the character (e.g., "aa28"). "Doll" Paperdoll System (3D Model). Complete block controlling character race, face shape, hair, and accessories. "Blueprint" Character Blueprint (UUID). Defines the unique identifier of the character within the game system.
Because directly writing UUIDs and appearance parameters by hand is extremely error-prone, follow this "borrowing a corpse to bring the soul back" replacement workflow:

Open the game and use the system's character creation tool (or recruit a new mercenary) to craft the desired "ideal companion appearance and portrait." Save the game after entering, generating a temporary new save file. Extract party.json from this new save, locate the new character's "Blueprint", "Doll" block, and "m_CustomPortrait" block, and copy them to another text file for backup.
documents.s: Step 1: Generate Legal New Appearance Data

documents.t: Extract party.json from the "main progress save" you want to modify. Search for the name of the companion you want to modify (using "CustomName") to locate that companion's "Descriptor" block. Replace the companion's original corresponding blocks with the copied "Doll" and "m_CustomPortrait".
documents.s: Step 2: Transfer Data to Target Save

documents.t: In the JSON structure, there will be many system-generated serial number tags (e.g., "$id": "644"). Must Not Duplicate: All values with "$id" in the block you copied must not duplicate any other $id in the entire party.json file. Solution: Feel free to change the numbers of these $ids (e.g., change them to "999644"), as long as they are unique within this file; they do not need to be in sequential order.
documents.s: Step 3: Handle Internal Reference IDs $id (Extremely Important)

documents.t: The game system relies on UUIDs to verify "who is whose pet." If this link is broken, the pet will become masterless or disappear from the party entirely. After modifying, be sure to check the following correspondences: In the "Master's" Descriptor block: "m_Pet": { "m_UniqueId": "Must fill in the pet character's UUID here" } In the "Pet (Companion's)" Descriptor block: "Master": { "m_UniqueId": "Must fill in the master character's UUID here" } (Note: UUIDs must never conflict with built-in NPC UUIDs in the game, which is why Step 1 recommends using in-game tools to create a new character to obtain a safe UUID.)

Emperor's New Clothes BUG: The 3D paperdoll models replaced using this method will appear without clothes in-game. Current Hypothesis: "ClothesPrimaryIndex" and "ClothesSecondaryIndex" inside the "Doll" block only define colors, while the actual declaration block for "wearing equipment and clothes" is missing or not correctly applied. If the equipment binding block (Equipment Definition) is found in the saves later, this entry will be updated.
tip Actually, once you trick out your skeleton followers, you hardly need to bring other companions along on adventures anymore, because it's like having your own five-person squad built-in....
documents.s: "Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous" Lich Skeleton Companion Save Editing Guide

documents.t: Since generating all followers directly with newly created characters hasn't been tested yet, for the first version it's recommended to keep things simpler by modifying mercenaries for the other three after the first MythicSkeletonCompanion (which generates automatically). The recommended operation workflow is as follows: Use ToyBox to add the MythicSkeletonCompanion Feat (any class branch works). In-game, recreate a companion appearance and portrait that you like. Edit the save JSON, pasting the companion appearance section and portrait of your favorite character into the corresponding companion data. Recruit three additional mercenaries in-game. Add the other three MythicSkeletonCompanion Feats. Modify the save file to map the corresponding mercenary's UniqueId to the Feat, m_pet, and add these three UniqueIds into the Master's definition. * Latest confirmation: only defining the Master and Pet relationship is required.

Category UUID Archer 0cebe3b375b6397438909ac9752d9792 Dual Wielder d4583662450245446ae3a56e07232e6f Tank 048456cce79943f4c9c9eec1aa5ce9a0 Two-Handed d4583662450245446ae3a56e07232e6 Updated 2026-11-27 In the table above, the UUID for Two-Handed was only 31 digits long and shared the exact same prefix as Dual Wielder (likely due to missing the last digit during recording or miscopying). Before proceeding, please search and confirm the correct Feat Blueprint GUID in-game using ToyBox's Search 'N Pick. Additionally, the #在m_part內加上 comment in the first line of the JSON examples below is a reminder note for the insertion location; please do not paste # comment lines into the official JSON when editing save files (such as party.json).

Add Appearance Definition​ #Add inside m_part { "$id": "6", "$type": "Kingmaker.UnitLogic.Parts.UnitPartDollData, Assembly-CSharp", "Default": { "$id": "7", "EquipmentEntityIds": [ "7368eafa3f5ee9d4bb9739b80faefdc3", "9ab83dd3a06ba6a4e97900bd6ffc4aab", "7c55ae7f07c9d4741b4837bd305d3ec0", "b8b615fabc0f7af448fb68f009113c61", "8a008a34d7462524c9b96132a28bb606" ], "EntityRampIdices": { "7c55ae7f07c9d4741b4837bd305d3ec0": 15, "861171cdd3930a84faab08ab85ba924a": 8, "7368eafa3f5ee9d4bb9739b80faefdc3": 8, "9ab83dd3a06ba6a4e97900bd6ffc4aab": 15 }, "EntitySecondaryRampIdices": {}, "Gender": "Female", "RacePreset": "ee326fab8804493499ce07c5cd8759e2", "ClothesPrimaryIndex": 9, "ClothesSecondaryIndex": 9 } } Change Portrait​ "Descriptor": { ... "UISettings": { "$id": "2694", "m_AlreadyAutomaticallyAdded": [], "m_CustomPortrait": { "$id": "2695", "m_CustomPortraitId": "B28894B2200AAE6300A928653E91CD2B" }, "m_Slots": {} }, ... },

documents.t: Feat Data Format (No Longer Needs Modification)​ { "$id": "109", "$type": "Kingmaker.UnitLogic.Feature, Assembly-CSharp", "m_Context": { "AssociatedBlueprint": "048456cce79943f4c9c9eec1aa5ce9a0", "m_OwnerRef": "e51cd2f4-f8e6-4956-93a7-86281cd5e92a", "m_Params": null }, "Blueprint": "048456cce79943f4c9c9eec1aa5ce9a0", "UniqueId": "e731dd8b-31cc-4114-9dd5-650a8672ddf0", "AttachTime": "12:00:47.3910000", "IsActive": true, "Components": { "$AddPet$858ef2c0-f8cf-41f4-af45-0bb06f90fa00": { "$type": "Kingmaker.EntitySystem.EntityFactComponentDelegate`2+ComponentRuntime[[Kingmaker.EntitySystem.Entities.UnitEntityData, Assembly-CSharp, Version=0.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=null],[Kingmaker.UnitLogic.FactLogic.AddPetData, Assembly-CSharp, Version=0.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=null]], Assembly-CSharp, Version=0.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=null", "m_Data": { "$id": "110", "SpawnedPetRef": "b27cd89c-a8b0-4a1c-a5f0-379c5e5fd9c3", "Disabled": false } } } }, Basically, as long as the Feat is added, you can search for the corresponding UUID in the save file to find the corresponding Section (only one structure like the above paragraph will exist). The previous approach was to paste the UUID of the mercenary (or corresponding character) into the "SpawnedPetRef" field (the value for this item in the second added Feat will be null). Part Relationship Configuration​ Part Section for the Character Becoming a Companion​ #Add inside m_part { "$id": "2459", "$type": "Kingmaker.UnitLogic.Parts.UnitPartPet, Assembly-CSharp", "m_MasterRef": { "m_Ref": "e51cd2f4-f8e6-4956-93a7-86281cd5e92a" }, "Type": "MythicSkeletalChampion" }, The m_Ref under m_MasterRef needs to be confirmed as the Master's (Feat owner's) UUID. Part Section for the Master​ #Add inside m_part { "$id": "10", "$type": "Kingmaker.UnitLogic.Parts.UnitPartPetMaster, Assembly-CSharp", "m_Pets": [ { "m_Ref": "b27cd89c-a8b0-4a1c-a5f0-379c5e5fd9c3" }, { "m_Ref": "46694232-fba8-4a18-8daa-1a1c933290e2" }, { "m_Ref": "14547546-c716-4e63-9a5c-d8126e9c01f6" }, { "m_Ref": "2577f7e3-a782-439d-90df-eaa70a440af4" } ], "m_ExPets": [] } Following the example above, add each companion's m_Ref definition into the m_Pets array to correctly bind multiple companions under the master character.

documents.t: Many users encounter 401 Unauthorized or repeated password prompts when connecting legacy clients like Ultrasonic: Core Cause (Plaintext Token vs. MD5 Salt Hash): Early Subsonic API versions used direct password transmission or outdated SHA1 authentication (Updated 2026-11-27: Early Subsonic API transmitted passwords in plaintext p= or simple Hex encoding p=enc:..., rather than SHA1); whereas modern Subsonic / OpenSubsonic API specifications require the Token + Salt (token=md5(password+salt)) pattern. Ultrasonic has a lower maintenance frequency and has compatibility issues handling OpenSubsonic extended specifications and specific URL escaping, causing the authorization header sent to Navidrome to not match expectations. Troubleshooting: In client connection settings, look for and check "Use Token Authentication" or force select Subsonic API 1.16+. It is recommended to directly use modern clients that have been actively maintained by the community in recent years.
documents.s: 4. Why Does Ultrasonic Easily Run into Issues? Subsonic Authentication Mechanism Explained

documents.t: Navidrome itself features a modern WebUI, but if you need offline caching, gapless playback, and Android Auto / CarPlay support in cars, the following clients are recommended:

Client Name Licensing Model Core Features Applicable Scenarios Symfonium Paid (Buyout) Excellent UI (Material You), gapless playback, Android Auto support, full local offline caching, advanced equalizer (EQ), built-in online lyrics auto-fetching Android experience ceiling, recommended as primary choice Tempo Open Source / Free Minimalist and smooth, intuitive operation, supports offline sync and gapless playback Top choice for those who love a clean interface DSub Open Source / Free Traditional classic, high stability, strong offline management, early Android-style UI Users who prefer a retro and stable style Substreamer Free Modern interface, integrated Chromecast casting, supports offline downloading Balanced choice among free options

Client Name Licensing Model Core Features Applicable Scenarios Arpeggi Free / In-app purchase donation UI closely matches Apple Music native design style, great fluidity Top recommended choice for iOS Amperfy Open Source / Free Supports Apple Watch standalone playback, CarPlay, background downloads Heavy users of the Apple ecosystem play:Sub Paid Long-standing veteran tool, detailed cache management, but UI has an older feel Hardcore players pursuing full feature sets

Sonixd (Updated 2026-11-27: Sonixd has been discontinued and rewritten by the same author as Feishin) / Feishin: An Electron-based modern cross-platform player with a UI layout comparable to Spotify, supporting real-time lyrics, global multimedia shortcuts, and local audio resampling. Supersonic: An ultra-lightweight desktop client written in Go, with extremely fast startup speed and very low memory consumption.

Navidrome is a server that heavily relies on ID3 audio tags, not depending on folder structures for categorization at the bottom layer, but reading audio metadata directly. Although Lidarr does not come with a built-in lyrics fetching module, you can build a complete automated closed-loop of "Download -> Auto Tag -> Auto Fetch Synchronized Dynamic Lyrics (.lrc) -> Instantly Trigger Navidrome Scan" through Lidarr Custom Scripts or Independent Sidecar Containers.
documents.s: 6. Music Library Tagging, Lidarr Automated Management, and Lyrics Download Organization

documents.t: Lidarr integrates the MusicBrainz database, automatically completing standardized tagging and file renaming when importing music: Enable Audio File Tag Writing (Media Management): Go to Lidarr Settings -> Media Management. Check Write Audio Tags: Set to Sync or Scrub and Sync. Key Checkboxes: Check Write Embedded Cover Art (embeds high-res cover art into files) and Save Artwork to Album Folder (generates folder.jpg / cover.jpg, which Navidrome will preferentially read as cache thumbnails). Standardized Renaming Structure (Naming): Enable Rename Tracks. Artist Folder Format: {Artist CleanName} Album Folder Format: {Artist CleanName} - {Release Year} - {Album CleanTitle} Track File Format: {Track:00} - {Track CleanTitle}
documents.s: 6.1 Lidarr Backend Automatic Standardization Settings (Replacing Manual Tag Editing)

documents.t: Approach A: Lidarr Integration with Custom Script (Most Elegant: Fully Automated Trigger Upon Import)​ Community open-source tools (such as synclyr2metadata) can be packaged into a single static binary and seamlessly embedded into the Lidarr container: Get the Tool: Place the compiled static executable into Lidarr's mounted directory, for example /opt/appdata/lidarr/scripts/synclyr2metadata. chmod +x /opt/appdata/lidarr/scripts/synclyr2metadata Configure Custom Script in Lidarr: Go to Lidarr Settings -> Connect -> Click + to add Custom Script. Name: Auto Sync Lyrics Triggers: Check On Release Import and On Upgrade. Path: Enter the container-internal path /config/scripts/synclyr2metadata. Workflow Mechanism: Whenever Lidarr downloads and organizes a new album, the script automatically requests synchronized lyrics from the largest open lyrics repository LRCLIB using the audio's Artist/Title/Duration, and directly writes them into the audio file's embedded LYRICS / SYLT tags (or outputs a same-named .lrc file). Approach B: Deploying an Independent Lyrics Fetching Container (LRCGET-CLI / LyricFlow)​ If you prefer not to put scripts inside Lidarr, you can mount a dedicated lyrics fetching sidecar service in Docker Compose (e.g., using the official lrcget-cli developed based on LRCLIB): Add to docker-compose.yml: lrcget: image: diegoninja/lrcget-cli:latest container_name: lrcget-cli restart: unless-stopped environment: - TZ=Asia/Taipei volumes: - /mnt/nas/music:/music:rw # Requires write permissions to store .lrc lyric files # Can also set scheduled scan jobs It will automatically monitor new audio under the /music directory, automatically generating same-named Song.lrc dynamic scrolling lyric files in the same directory.
documents.s: 6.2 Dynamic Lyrics Auto-Fetching and Organization Solutions (Two Mainstream Approaches)

documents.t: Navidrome scans periodically according to ND_SCANSCHEDULE by default (e.g., every 1 hour). Through Lidarr's Webhook integration, you can immediately trigger a partial Navidrome scan the moment a new album is downloaded and organized: Go to Lidarr Settings -> Connect -> Click + to add Webhook. URL: http://navidrome:4533/rest/startScan?u=<admin_user>&t=<token>&s=<salt>&v=1.16.1&c=Lidarr Triggers: Check On Download and On Upgrade. (Token and Salt generation methods follow the Subsonic API standard: token=md5(password+salt)).
documents.s: 6.3 Closed-Loop Automation: Lidarr Download Complete Automatically Notifying Navidrome to Refresh

documents.t: For older local collections or rare self-recorded audio not included in the Lidarr monitoring workflow, it is recommended to use MusicBrainz Picard for manual organization before throwing them into the NAS, cleaning up standard Title, Artist, Album Artist, Track Number, and Date fields before archiving.

After separating /music (NAS remote library) and /data (local SSD), data backup only requires backing up the lightweight local directory: # Backup Navidrome database and playback history sudo tar -czvf /opt/backups/navidrome-$(date +%F).tar.gz -C /opt/navidrome data # Restoration method sudo tar -xzvf /opt/backups/navidrome-*.tar.gz -C /opt/navidrome/ sudo chown -R 1000:1000 /opt/navidrome/data docker compose restart navidrome

tip In Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous (WotR), the pet/companion system received a low-level refactoring. Through save editing, we can not only bypass single-pet restrictions but also exploit system logic vulnerabilities to transform "Mercenaries"—who feature complete paper dolls, independent equipment slots, and upgrade trees—into "Hidden Companions" that do not consume the 6-person party limit.
documents.s: Breaking Party Size Limits: ToyBox Settings and Mercenary-to-Companion Save Modification

documents.t: Rather than risking corrupted saves by performing high-difficulty code dissection and porting inside dense JSON files, the safest and most direct correct solution is to directly lift the party size limit. Enabling the ToyBox mod in-game saves you countless hours of debugging: Go to the Party tab in ToyBox. Locate and increase the Party Size limit (e.g., set to 8 or 10 people). Head to the tavern to hire a large number of mercenaries normally to form a legion. Advantage Analysis: The system automatically handles all legitimate class progression trees, independent equipment slots, and combat death/resurrection checks. It completely avoids vicious bugs brought by JSON modifications while maintaining maximum freedom in party composition and immersion.
documents.s: 💡 Core Conclusion: ToyBox Party Limit Lift (Best Practice)

documents.t: If you remain curious about the engine's low-level limits, here are the verified engine mechanics: Topic Explored Engine Low-Level Determination and Conclusion Can there be up to six companions? Limited by UI and stability. The underlying layer can accommodate countless entities, but when the total party entities exceed 14 to 16, party portraits break, and turn-based mode easily triggers timeline freezes. Can multiple types of companions coexist? Completely correct. Animal companions, mythic skeleton warriors, and Azata dragon companions occupy different system slots and stack perfectly on the same master. Can you bring one of each animal/skeleton? The system follows a uniqueness rule. Forcibly adding duplicate identical feats causes entities to overwrite each other or breaks the level-up interface. Building a skeleton army or zoo requires the "Mercenary to Companion" exploit. Penalty for forced companion conversion without feats If the master lacks the corresponding feat and the JSON is forcibly modified, the companion's experience points will be permanently frozen, permanent vaporization occurs upon respec, and automatic resurrection upon death is unavailable.
This section is intended only for hardcore players who want to challenge engine limits and pursue keeping characters off the party bar at the top of the screen.
documents.s: ⚙️ [Technical Supplement] Save Low-Level Modification and Mercenary Conversion SOP

documents.t: Save Path: C:\Users\{Username}\AppData\LocalLow\Owlcat Games\Pathfinder Wrath Of The Righteous\Saved Games Save Format: .zks files are standard ZIP archives; always back up before modifying. Windows Tools: Notepad++ with the Jstool Plug-in is recommended, using the JSFormat function to align the JSON tree structure. Linux Tools: Notepadqq is recommended. Terminal formatting command: cat file.json | python -m json.tool > new.json

To avoid bugs like level-up UI crashes and respec vaporization, we must borrow a legitimate pet's "household registration" (slot) and graft the mercenary's "body." Step 1: Obtain Registration and Body Hire a brand new mercenary at the tavern in-game, setting up appearance and class. Open ToyBox, navigate to Party -> Features, and forcibly grant the master an animal feat they would never normally use (e.g., centipede) to let the system legally generate a pet. Change maps to spawn the entity, then save and exit. Step 2: Free Up Party Space Extract the .zks save and open player.json. Locate the "m_Party" array and remove the mercenary's UUID from it. Step 3: Data Porting and Overwriting Open party.json and locate the block for the "centipede (legitimate pet)." Take "Doll" (3D appearance), "m_Inventory" (equipment slots), "m_Slots" (equipment nodes), and "Stats" (base attributes) from the mercenary block, and overwrite the corresponding blocks of the centipede. Never overwrite the centipede's "Blueprint" and "Progression" (animal progression trees must be retained). Once done, completely delete the original mercenary's large standalone block. Step 4: Master-Servant Bidirectional Binding In the "Descriptor" block of the synthesized entity (the original centipede), locate the "Master" field and enter the master's UUID. Search for the master's name, find the "m_Pets" array, and confirm the synthesized entity's UUID is present within it. Pack the JSON back into .zks and enter the game.
documents.s: Implementation SOP: Body Snatching Method (Precise Organ Transplant)

documents.t: Abnormal Situation System Reason and Solution Companion vanishes or turns hostile Definitely a Master binding failure or incorrect UUID in party.json. The system treats the entity as wild wildlife. Mercenary companion cutscene freezes Special cinematic cutscenes strictly check party positioning, which may cause model misalignment. Press Esc to skip or change maps to recover. Unable to open mercenary companion inventory UI determination exception. Open ToyBox, check Allow Equip Everything and Show Inventory for All under the Bag of Tricks tab to forcibly unlock.

While not an elegant solution, it is a workaround since the exact check condition couldn't be found, allowing him to join as early as after the Chapter 2 mission.

documents.t: This represents the architecture of my HomeLab, continuously refined over the years, reflecting the current equilibrium among requirements, electricity costs, and hardware expenses. It is archived here for reference, and anyone interested in setting up a similar architecture is welcome to exchange ideas.

Minimum Actual Cost Considering budget and electricity bills, it is impractical to run family services across a fleet of physical machines. The physical foundation of the entire setup essentially consists of one Tower Server + one legacy physical NAS + a complimentary OCI Free Tier cloud instance. Maximum Functional Atomization Having suffered through the early pain of stuffing various services onto a single host—resulting in tangled dependencies and debugging nightmares—I have fully adopted containerization and applied strict isolation to hosts based on security levels and usage requirements. Satisfying Digital Hoarding I am a digital hoarder. Lacking the funds to stockpile enterprise-grade hardware every day, I stockpile digital data. Therefore, the overall architecture might not be pristine or minimalist, but capacity and data classification are definitely well-covered. Satisfying Quirky Vanity I am aware there are many out-of-the-box turnkey solutions or commercial software options available to easily fulfill requirements, but unfortunately, I am an old-school person living in the 2000s: If I can hardcode it with FreeBSD, I will never buy a ready-made router; if I can hardcode it with Linux, I will never pay for a subscription service.

documents.t: Symbol Name Core Function & Behavior Analysis Practical Command Examples $ Variable Value Symbol Extracts the value corresponding to a variable, also used for environment variables or special variables (e.g., $?, $$). echo $USER echo $? (Returns the exit status code of the previous command) # Comment Symbol A # at the beginning of a line or after a space denotes a comment; the shell directly ignores everything after it. # This is a comment mkdir app # Create a directory \ Escape Character Removes the special semantics of the immediately following single character, restoring it to literal text; or acts as a line continuation character. echo \$PATH rm -f filename\ with\ space.txt | Pipe Symbol Redirects the "standard output (stdout)" of the left-hand command into the "standard input (stdin)" of the right-hand command. cat access.log | grep "404" | wc -l ; Command Separator Executes multiple commands sequentially in a row (the next command executes regardless of whether the previous one succeeded). cd /opt; ls -la; df -h & Background Execution Job Control Moves a command to run in the background, immediately releasing the current terminal prompt. python3 server.py & nohup ./backup.sh & / Directory Path Separator The directory level separator in the Linux virtual file system tree structure; a single / at the very top represents the root directory. /var/log/docker.log > Output Redirection (Overwrite) Redirects and writes standard output to the specified file, overwriting it directly if the file already exists. echo "token=123" > config.env >> Output Redirection (Append) Redirects and writes standard output to the specified file, appending to the very end of the file without overwriting. date >> /var/log/deploy.log < Input Redirection Uses the contents of the specified file as the standard input for a command (replacing keyboard input). mysql -u root -p db < backup.sql << Here-Document Defines a multi-line text block as standard input until a custom delimiter tag (such as EOF) is encountered. cat << 'EOF' > test.txt hello EOF ' ' Single Quotes (Strong Quoting) Completely maintains literal characters, internal variables and escape sequences are not evaluated at all. echo '$USER' (Output: $USER) " " Double Quotes (Weak Quoting) Preserves most text, but allows evaluation of variables ($), command substitution ($()), and escapes (\). echo "Hi, $USER" (Output: Hi, admin) $( ) or ` ` Command Substitution Evaluates the commands inside the brackets first and substitutes their execution result (stdout) back into the original location. TODAY=$(date +%F) tar -czvf "backup-$TODAY.tar.gz" /data ( ) Subshell Executes a group of commands in an independently forked sub-process; directory changes or variable assignments inside it will not pollute the outer layer. (cd /tmp && rm -rf *) (Current shell remains in the original directory after execution completes) { } Command Group / Expansion 1. Groups and executes commands in the current shell (requires spaces and semicolons). 2. Batch expands sequences/strings. { echo 1; echo 2; } mkdir -p /opt/{app,db,config} cp app.yml{,.bak}

documents.t: Wildcards are primarily expanded by the shell before executing commands (Pathname Expansion), used for matching filenames and paths: Wildcard Matching Rule Precise Behavior Analysis Practical Examples * 0 to arbitrary characters Matches strings of arbitrary length in a filename (excluding leading dots . for hidden files). ls *.log (Lists all files ending in .log) rm -rf /tmp/cache* ? Exactly 1 arbitrary character Must and can only match 1 character (cannot be 0, cannot exceed 1). ls file?.txt (Matches file1.txt, fileA.txt, but does not match file10.txt) [abc] Any character within the set Matches any single character listed inside the brackets. ls report_[abc].pdf (Matches report_a.pdf, report_b.pdf, etc.) [0-9] Any character within an encoded range Matches any character within a continuous ASCII / character encoding range. ls img_[0-9].png (Matches single digits 0 through 9) ls [a-z]*.md (Files starting with a lowercase letter) [!abc] (or [^abc]) Excluded set (Negation) Any single character excluding those specified inside the brackets. ls file[!0-9].txt (Matches fileA.txt, excludes file1.txt)

cmd1 && cmd2 (AND): Executes cmd2 only if cmd1 executes successfully (Exit Code = 0). cmd1 || cmd2 (OR): Executes cmd2 only if cmd1 fails to execute (Exit Code ≠ 0). Classic Example: docker compose pull && docker compose up -d || echo "Deployment update failed!"

Shell Wildcards (Globbing): Evaluated by the shell, mapped directly to filenames on disk. * represents "arbitrary string". ? represents "single character". Regular Expressions (Regex): Evaluated by specific tools (grep, sed, awk, python), used for matching text content. * represents "the preceding character repeated 0 or more times". . represents "any single character". .* The combination of both equals the wildcard *.

Quickly create a backup file (equivalent to cp nginx.conf nginx.conf.bak) cp nginx.conf{,.bak} # 3. Two-dimensional matrix expansion (generates a1, a2, b1, b2) echo {a,b}{1,2}

The basic format of an escape sequence is: \e[<style/color code>m \e[ (or \033[, \x1b[): CSI (Control Sequence Introducer) prefix. <code>: Style code. Multiple codes can be chained with a semicolon ; (for example, \e[1;31;40m represents bold + red text + black background). m: Select Graphic Rendition (SGR) terminator. \e[0m: Reset control sequence. If you do not reset at the end, all subsequent text in the terminal will retain that color!

# Using echo (requires -e) echo -e "\e[1;31m[ERROR]\e[0m Server connection failed" # Recommended POSIX-standard approach (printf, no -e needed and fully portable across platforms) printf "\033[1;32m[SUCCESS]\033[0m Deployment completed\n"
