documents.s: KDE Plasma Post-Login Freezes, Black Screen Delays, and Session Corruption

documents.t: No matter which Linux distribution you use (Arch, Fedora, Ubuntu, or openSUSE), as long as your desktop environment is KDE Plasma 5 or Plasma 6, after experiencing a system update, graphics driver change, or abnormal shutdown, you may occasionally encounter the following typical desktop crash symptoms: Long Black Screen Waiting After Login: After entering your password in SDDM or GDM, the screen directly turns black and freezes for 10 to 30 seconds. The mouse pointer can move, but desktop components and the taskbar fail to appear. Forced Pop-up of Historical Windows: Even if "Start with an empty session" is checked in system settings, every boot still forcefully restores all terminals, browsers, or specific software running before the last shutdown. Delayed Loading or Disappearance of the Panel: After the black screen ends, the taskbar may take several seconds to emerge, or even completely fail to respond to right-click menus.
documents.s: 1. Incident Inventory: The Long Black Screen and Ghost Windows After Login

documents.t: KDE Plasma internally relies on ksmserver and plasmashell to manage sessions. When the system encounters a crash, display server (X11/Wayland) restart, or driver context anomaly, the status files responsible for recording window geometric states and GPU contexts easily become corrupted or locked as read-only. This leads to two chain reactions: GUI Switches Are Bypassed: Although the system settings interface displays "empty session", the underlying daemon still forcibly reads the corrupted old session files. Triggering the 20-Second Timeout Protection Mechanism: When plasmashell boots, it frantically attempts in the background to rebuild those old windows carrying invalid GPU resources until the Session Manager's connection timeout protection mechanism is triggered, after which the desktop components tardily load.
documents.s: 2. Root Cause Analysis: Why is Disabling Restoration in GUI Settings Ineffective?

documents.t: Since the GUI settings have failed, the most direct and effective approach is to issue commands from the terminal to thoroughly erase corrupted status files and desktop composition caches. Erase Session Restoration Status Files Configuration file paths vary slightly across Plasma versions; execute the following commands to clear both old and new specification session records together: # Delete Plasma 6 session restoration state file rm -f ~/.local/state/plasmasessionrestorestaterc # Delete Plasma 5 / 6 legacy session directory rm -rf ~/.config/session/* Clear Desktop Components and Window Manager Cache Corrupted QML cache or KWin effect cache can similarly slow down loading speeds: # Clear temporary files for plasmashell and kwin rm -rf ~/.cache/plasmashell* rm -rf ~/.cache/kwin* rm -rf ~/.cache/plasma* Restart to Verify After performing the above cleanup, reboot the computer or log out: systemctl reboot Verification Indicator: After entering the password in SDDM, wallpapers and the taskbar should instantly load within 1 to 3 seconds, and no residual windows from the previous session should pop up.
documents.s: 3. Forceful Reset: Clearing Corrupted Sessions and Caches

documents.t: If delays persist after clearing the cache, the problem most likely lies in background user services (Systemd User Services) that launch alongside Plasma: # Check which user-level services slowed down the boot process during startup systemd-analyze --user blame If you find specific custom scripts or third-party synchronization tools (such as specific cloud sync software, IME daemons) taking abnormal amounts of time, you can temporarily exclude them using systemctl --user disable <service_name>.
documents.s: 4. Advanced Troubleshooting: Check Systemd User Services If Sluggishness Persists

documents.t: Hope for escaping corporate IT system shackles​ Important node for managing HomeLab from the office​ VPN Console connecting back home from the office​ As the name implies, WSL is Linux running on Windows. Through WSL, I can install tools that my company does not allow me to install, and connect back home via VPN to use it as a springboard or directly as a terminal. Naturally, the distribution running inside WSL is my favorite—Arch Linux.
WireGuard​ Desktop Tools​ Remote Desktop Client​

info This article was automatically translated by Google "Gemini". The author does not guarantee its accuracy or wording. tip Since Microsoft introduced the Store version of WSL (version 1.0 and above), the biggest advantage is native systemd support and much better integration with GUI Apps (WSLg). This article records how to set up the core WSL environment from scratch and switch the distribution to my preferred Arch Linux (ArchWSL).
documents.s: WSL (Store Version) Installation and ArchWSL Initialization Setup

documents.t: Windows System Version Verification Minimum Requirements: Windows 10 version 2004 and later (Build 19041 and above) or Windows 11. How to Check Version: Press Win + R and type winver. Windows 10 Note: To fully support the latest WSL features, Windows 10 generally requires update KB5020030. If your system does not update automatically, you can search and download it from the Microsoft Update Catalog according to your platform. (Updated 2026-11-27: KB5020030 has been superseded by subsequent cumulative updates, and Windows 10 reached end of life (EOL) on October 14, 2025; it is recommended to use Windows 11 directly.)
There are two ways to install WSL now. Using the command line is recommended for speed, but you can also use the GUI if you prefer:

Open PowerShell with administrator privileges and enter: wsl --install This command will automatically enable all necessary Windows features and install Ubuntu by default. If you want to enable the features without installing Ubuntu, you can append the --no-distribution flag. Reboot your system after the process finishes.

If you prefer manually confirming features or downloading from the Microsoft Store: Search for WSL in the Microsoft Store and install it. Open "Turn Windows features on or off". Ensure the following core components are checked: Hyper-V: This must be enabled. (Updated 2026-11-27: Running WSL 2 does not require enabling the full Hyper-V role, and Windows Home editions do not have this option.) Windows Hypervisor Platform (Updated 2026-11-27: This option is intended for third-party emulators/virtual machines and is not a required component for WSL 2.) Windows Subsystem for Linux: The core component for WSL. Virtual Machine Platform: Required for WSL 2. Reboot your computer after configuration.

Using Windows Terminal (also available in the Store) is strongly recommended when working with WSL. Customization Tip: Remember to install the Nerd Fonts family and set it as the font in Windows Terminal settings. This ensures that when you use zsh with themes like powerlevel10k inside WSL, those fancy icons and status bars won't render as garbled characters (essentially required for any customized environment).

Since I am not fond of the built-in WSL distributions (mostly Debian/Ubuntu derivatives), I chose to use ArchWSL. Installation Usage: Very simple; you can now open the Microsoft Store, search for ArchWSL (or Arch Linux), and click get and install. After installation, launch it directly from the start menu to perform initial environment initialization. Compared to downloading and extracting archives from GitHub manually in the past, installing and managing through the Microsoft Store is much more convenient. (Updated 2026-11-27: yuk7/ArchWSL is a third-party GitHub project rather than an official Microsoft Store listing; official native Arch Linux WSL images are now available and can be installed directly in PowerShell via wsl --install archlinux.)

After installing ArchWSL via the Store, we need to verify and manually enable systemd support inside WSL by following these steps: 1. Check WSL Version Enter the following in Windows PowerShell or CMD: wsl --version Confirm that the version number is displayed and is Store version (1.0.0 or higher). 2. Check and Modify WSL Configuration File Enter your ArchWSL terminal and ensure /etc/wsl.conf exists and contains the following lines: [boot] systemd=true 3. Restart and Verify Go back to Windows PowerShell, completely shut down WSL, and restart it: wsl --shutdown wsl After re-entering WSL, run the following command to check the PID 1 process: ps --no-headers -o comm 1 If systemd is displayed on the screen, it was successful!

Since Hyper-V and the Virtual Machine Platform are enabled, if you also use VirtualBox, you might encounter issues where virtual machines fail to start. The solution is simple: go to the VM settings in VirtualBox, navigate to "System" -> "Acceleration", and change the Paravirtualization Interface to Hyper-V.
Once the core environment and Arch distribution are set up, more detailed WSL development environments and network configurations will be covered in the next article.

info This article was automatically translated by Google "Gemini". The author does not guarantee its accuracy or wording. tip WSL can now run virtual machines by enabling Nested Virtualization as a passthrough Hypervisor. Simply put, WSL2 itself is already a virtual machine running on Windows Hyper-V. By enabling this feature, we can run QEMU/KVM virtual machines inside WSL2, achieving a "virtual machine inside a virtual machine" effect (though performance will naturally degrade).
documents.s: Guide to Enabling QEMU/KVM Nested Virtualization and Virt-Manager in WSL2

documents.t: Ivon's Blog - Linux enables nested virtualization, running virtual machines inside virtual machines: https://www.google.com/search?q=https://ivonblog.com/posts/wsl2-nested-virtualization/ (Updated 2026-11-27: Original link mistakenly used Google search redirect URL, please visit https://ivonblog.com/posts/wsl2-nested-virtualization/ directly) Ivon's Blog - Spice Guest Tools usage, QEMU/KVM VM auto-scaling resolution and shared folders (Current link points to site homepage) Ivon's Blog - VirtIO-Balloon: Flexible RAM, QEMU/KVM dynamic memory allocation for virtual machines (Current link points to site homepage) Installing QEMU/KVM and Virt Manager virtual machine software on Arch Linux (Current link points to site homepage)

1. Update WSL Kernel Ensure your WSL is up to date by running in Windows PowerShell: wsl --update 2. Enable Nested Virtualization ⚠️ Common Pitfall Reminder: Nested virtualization settings apply to the entire WSL2 virtual machine engine and must therefore be written in the global Windows configuration file .wslconfig, not inside WSL's internal /etc/wsl.conf. Open Windows File Explorer, edit or create C:\Users\<YourUsername>\.wslconfig, and add the following section: [wsl2] nestedVirtualization=true Once done, force restart WSL in PowerShell to apply the settings: wsl --shutdown

Updated 2026-11-27 In addition to the third-party ArchWSL, Arch Linux now provides an official WSL2 image (archlinux-wsl), which can be installed directly in Windows via wsl --install archlinux. Before executing systemctl enable --now libvirtd below, you must ensure that WSL's internal /etc/wsl.conf has configured systemd=true under the [boot] section and restarted via wsl --shutdown, otherwise systemctl will not function. After restarting and entering WSL (Arch Linux), begin installing virtualization-related tools. 1. Install Core and Network Packages sudo pacman -S archlinux-keyring qemu-full virt-manager virt-viewer edk2-ovmf dnsmasq vde2 bridge-utils openbsd-netcat libguestfs iptables virglrenderer Updated 2026-11-27 ebtables has been removed from the official Arch Linux package repositories, and its functionality has been replaced by iptables supporting the nftables backend. Please remove ebtables when running pacman -S to avoid target not found errors. If you need the VirtioFS shared folder feature detailed in Section 4, please also install the virtiofsd package (split from QEMU into an independent package). 2. Install TPM 2.0 Emulation Package (If running Windows 11 Guest) sudo pacman -S swtpm 3. Start and Configure Libvirt Service # Start and enable libvirtd on boot sudo systemctl enable --now libvirtd # Start default virtual network (NAT) sudo virsh net-start default # Set virtual network to auto-start on boot sudo virsh net-autostart default 4. Adjust Account Permissions To avoid entering the root password every time you open Virt-Manager, add the current user to the relevant groups: sudo usermod -a -G libvirt $USER sudo usermod -a -G libvirt root sudo usermod -a -G kvm $USER sudo usermod -a -G kvm root Updated 2026-11-27 The root account inherently possesses full system permissions and does not require running usermod -a -G libvirt root and usermod -a -G kvm root. You only need to add the regular user $USER to the libvirt and kvm groups and re-login (or restart WSL). 5. Configure Polkit Rules (Passwordless Management) Edit /etc/polkit-1/rules.d/50-libvirt.rules: /* Allow users in kvm group to manage the libvirt daemon without authentication */ polkit.addRule(function(action, subject) { if (action.id == "org.libvirt.unix.manage" && subject.isInGroup("kvm")) { return polkit.Result.YES; } }); After making modifications, restart the service to apply permissions (safest is to log out of WSL and log back in, or run wsl --shutdown): sudo systemctl restart libvirtd
documents.s: II. Installing QEMU/KVM and Virt-Manager in ArchWSL

documents.t: Once you have installed a Guest OS (virtual machine) in Virt-Manager, you need to install enhancement packages similar to VMware Tools to enable auto-scaling windows and clipboard sharing. 1. Install QEMU and SPICE Guest Agents Run inside the Guest OS (inside the virtual machine): sudo pacman -S spice-vdagent qemu-guest-agent xf86-video-qxl If you are using an X11 desktop environment, you can install x-resize via AUR for window auto-scaling: yay -S x-resize 💡 Confusion Regarding Service Enable: Many older online tutorials state that you need to systemctl enable these services. However, modern spice-vdagent is usually automatically started by the desktop environment (such as GNOME / KDE / XFCE autostart), while qemu-guest-agent is triggered via socket. Therefore, not finding corresponding service files or not needing to manually enable them is normal; as long as the functionality works normally after rebooting.
documents.s: III. Guest OS Settings (Taking Arch Linux as a Second-Layer Example)

documents.t: Through VirtioFS, the Guest OS can natively and efficiently access folders on the Host (referring to WSL here). 1. Virt-Manager Hardware Configuration Shut down the Guest OS first. Click the "light bulb" icon on the top row of the Virt-Manager window (Show virtual hardware details). Click Add Hardware at the bottom left. Select Filesystem: Driver: Select virtiofs Source path: Enter the directory in WSL, e.g., /home/kiwi/host (remember to create this folder in WSL first) Target path: This is the Mount Tag, name it freely, e.g., host Click Finish and start the virtual machine. Updated 2026-11-27 Before using VirtioFS, you must also check Enable shared memory in the Memory page of the Virt-Manager virtual machine settings, otherwise starting the virtual machine will result in a virtiofs requires shared memory error. 2. Mounting in Guest OS Manual mount test: # -t virtiofs <Target Path Tag> <Mount point inside Guest OS> sudo mount -t virtiofs host /home/kiwi/host Write to /etc/fstab for auto-mount on boot: After confirming manual mounting works, edit /etc/fstab inside the Guest OS and add this line: # Shared Folder with HOST (WSL) # <Target Tag> <Mount Point> <Format> <Options> <dump> <pass> host /home/kiwi/host virtiofs rw,noatime,_netdev 0 2 Note: Adding the _netdev option ensures the system mounts after loading network and external device modules, preventing boot hangs. Updated 2026-11-27 The sixth column pass (fsck check order) is recommended to be set to 0 (i.e., 0 0) rather than 2, because virtiofs is a virtual shared filesystem and there is no corresponding fsck.virtiofs checking tool in the system.

info This article was automatically translated by Google "Gemini". The author does not guarantee its accuracy or wording. tip WSL allows users to load custom Linux Kernels by default. Because certain specific advanced applications (such as bridging networks or advanced traffic control when running QEMU/KVM virtual machines) often lack corresponding modules (like TC/QoS) in the official default kernel, compiling and configuring a custom WSL Kernel fills in these required functions.
documents.s: WSL2 Custom Linux Kernel Compilation and Replacement Guide

documents.t: macOS on WSL2 (Win10) — Docker-OSX — https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/sickcodes/Docker-OSX (Updated 2026-11-27: Removed Google search redirect prefix, restored original GitHub project URL) Accelerated KVM guests on WSL 2 — https://www.google.com/search?q=https://boxofcables.dev/accelerated-kvm-guests-on-wsl-2/ (Updated 2026-11-27: Removed Google search redirect prefix, restored original article URL) WSL2-Linux-Kernel (Microsoft GitHub) — https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/microsoft/WSL2-Linux-Kernel (Updated 2026-11-27: Removed Google search redirect prefix, restored original GitHub project URL) WSL2 自编译内核使用 tc qdisc (Updated 2026-11-27: Original link was an invalid placeholder URL with ellipses, unable to resolve target page) 如何編譯與更換WSL核心 (custom WSL kernel) (Updated 2026-11-27: Original link was an invalid placeholder URL, reference Microsoft official documentation Advanced settings configuration in WSL instead)

In Arch Linux (WSL), aside from basic base-devel, compiling the kernel requires tools like ncurses (for menuconfig), bc, flex, bison, pahole, and libelf: sudo pacman -S base-devel ncurses bc flex bison pahole libelf

Use Git to fetch Microsoft's open-source WSL Kernel source code. Tip: This assumes you want version 6.1.y. For other versions, refer to the branch names on the GitHub repo. Appending --depth=1 fetches only the latest commit, greatly saving download time and disk space. git clone https://github.com/microsoft/WSL2-Linux-Kernel.git --depth=1 -b linux-msft-wsl-6.1.y cd WSL2-Linux-Kernel Updated 2026-11-27 Modern newer WSL2 default kernels have evolved to version 6.6.y (branches such as linux-msft-wsl-6.6.y) and above; before compiling, it is recommended to check your current environment version with uname -r, then select the corresponding branch on WSL2-Linux-Kernel.
documents.s: 2. Obtain the WSL2 Linux Kernel Source Code

documents.t: Many tutorials recommend directly copying Microsoft/config-wsl from the WSL2-Linux-Kernel repo, but this is strongly discouraged. Why avoid the official config-wsl? You will find a large number of M (compiled as dynamically loadable modules) entries in the official file. In a WSL environment, if module paths and loading mechanisms are not specially configured, features set to M (such as WireGuard) will often fail to be found and will cease to work directly after replacing the custom kernel. Best Practice: Export Config from the Current System — Extracting the configuration from a stably running WSL Kernel is the safest approach; extracted configuration items default to * (Built-in, directly bundled into the kernel). You can use either of the following methods to export the configuration and save it as .config (placed in the root directory of the source code you just cloned): zcat /proc/config.gz > .config # or cat /proc/config.gz | gunzip > .config
documents.s: II. Preparing the Kernel Config File

documents.t: As recommended earlier, do not manually edit the .config text file because module dependencies exist, and manual edits easily lead to errors. Use the menuconfig tool instead: # If your file is named .config and located in the current directory, you can simply run make menuconfig make menuconfig KCONFIG_CONFIG=.config Add TC/QoS (Traffic Control / Quality of Service) Support: The reason for compiling manually this time is that the new QEMU package requires TC/QoS functionality. Once inside the text-based graphical interface, navigate to the following path and press Y on each item to turn them into * (Built-in) state: Networking support -> Network options -> QoS and/or fair queueing Once configured, select Save and exit.

After configuring and saving, you can begin compilation. We can directly specify compiling bzImage for greater precision: # Compile using all CPU cores on the system (fastest) make -j$(nproc) KCONFIG_CONFIG=.config bzImage # Of course, if you only want to allocate a specific number of cores (e.g., 16 cores), you can specify manually: make -j16 KCONFIG_CONFIG=.config bzImage Once compilation completes, your new kernel file will reside at: arch/x86/boot/bzImage
Copy the compiled bzImage to your preferred folder on the Windows host, such as C:\WSL_Kernel\bzImage.
documents.s: IV. Replacing and Using the Custom Kernel

documents.t: This is also the officially recommended and safest approach. Edit C:\Users\<Your_Username>\.wslconfig in Windows: Note: Backslashes \ in Windows paths must be escaped as \\ to take effect. # Main WSL Setting Section [wsl2] # Allow WSL to run Hypervisor features (Required for QEMU/KVM) nestedVirtualization=true # Specify the custom kernel file path kernel=C:\\WSL_Kernel\\bzImage # Limit WSL maximum RAM usage (units can be GB/MB) memory=16GB After configuration, run wsl --shutdown in PowerShell to forcibly close WSL; the next time it starts, your custom kernel will be loaded (you can verify the version with uname -r).
documents.s: Method A: Modify Global Setting .wslconfig (Strongly Recommended 🌟)

documents.t: The default path where Windows stores the WSL Kernel is: C:\Windows\system32\lxss\tools\kernel Updated 2026-11-27 C:\Windows\system32\lxss\tools\kernel only applies to older WSL versions built into early Windows systems; modern WSL installed and updated via the Microsoft Store (default architecture for Windows 10/11) places kernel files in the protected WindowsApps directory. Please always use Method A (.wslconfig) to load custom kernels. You can directly rename the compiled bzImage to kernel and drop it into this folder to overwrite it (requires administrator privileges, and WSL must be completely shut down beforehand). Disadvantage: Applies immediately without any configuration. Fatal Flaw: If your compiled kernel has a bug causing it to fail to boot, you won't even have the default rescue environment, making troubleshooting extremely difficult. Thus, this approach is extremely discouraged.
documents.s: Method B: Directly Overwrite the Windows Default Kernel (Extremely Discouraged ❌)

documents.t: Set up a personal Blog + Wiki using Hexo + GitHub Pages.

This leverages several features of GitHub Pages: Inside the <Username>.github.io repository's master (Updated 2026-11-27: GitHub's default main branch is now main, and modern GitHub Pages also allows specifying arbitrary branches or deploying directly via GitHub Actions) branch, the index.html file generates the valid URL https://<Username>.github.io/ In other repositories, GitHub Pages generates the valid URL https://<username>.github.io/<other-repo>/ from index.html within the gh-pages branch. Therefore, you can generate the blog's web pages into the main branch of the <username>.github.io repository to serve as the primary website, and generate web pages using other desired themes into the gh-pages branch of other repositories to serve as sub-sites. Although you can specify a particular _config.yml using Hexo commands to combine the two, the underlying principle is the same as the table above. However, doing so allows you to store the Hexo Wiki and Hexo Blog in the same directory, integrating Git synchronization management.
Hexo Official Documentation OHLIA's Wiki 別院牧志 風月 途探生靈
Hexo is a very simple and easy-to-use static page generator, essentially requiring npm + Node.js.

Linux​ Arch Series sudo pacman -S git Debian/Ubuntu Series sudo apt-get install git-core Updated 2026-11-27 git-core is an early obsolete transitional package name; modern Debian/Ubuntu environments should use sudo apt update && sudo apt install git directly. Since installing GitHub Desktop on Linux is somewhat cumbersome—especially without a VPN inside mainland China—it is recommended to just use Command Line git. If worst comes to worst, writing a script makes it very convenient anyway. Windows​ On Windows, it is recommended to directly download GitHub Desktop for convenience, which can be downloaded and installed from the official website or installed via Chocolatey: choco install github-desktop

Linux​ Arch Series sudo pacman -S nodejs npm Debian/Ubuntu Series sudo apt-get install -y nodejs npm Updated 2026-11-27 The Node.js version provided by default in Debian/Ubuntu apt repositories is typically older and may not meet the requirements of newer Hexo versions or frontend tooling. In practice, it is recommended to install LTS versions using nvm, fnm, or NodeSource. Windows​ Similar to GitHub Desktop, you can download and install it from Node.js, which includes npm bundled in, or install it via Chocolatey: choco install nodejs
Hexo is installed using npm. I have never installed it under Windows, but I assume it is the same: npm install -g hexo-cli It is installed once finished.

documents.t: Hexo's core settings are all stored in <folder>/_config.yml. Most defaults can be kept as-is, which is very convenient, and only a few items need to be adjusted as needed. Detailed Hexo Configuration

# Site title: Kiwi's Blog subtitle: 中年大叔的自言自語 description: '' keywords: author: Kiwi language: zh_TW timezone: Setting Description title Site title subtitle Site subtitle description Site description keywords Site keywords. Supports multiple keywords. author Your name language Language used by the site; refer to 2-letter ISO-639-1 code, defaults to en timezone Site timezone. Hexo uses your computer's timezone by default; you can find an appropriate timezone in the timezone list, such as America/New_York, Japan, and UTC

If your site is hosted in a subdirectory, such as http://example.org/blog, set your url to http://example.org/blog and set root to /blog/. # URL url: https://kiwi0093.github.io/ root: / permalink: :year/:month/:day/:title/ permalink_defaults: pretty_urls: trailing_index: true trailing_html: true Setting Description Default url Site URL, must start with http:// or https:// root Root directory of the site permalink Format of post permalinks :year/:month/:day/:title/ permalink_defaults Default values for each segment in permalink pretty_urls Rewrites permalink values to beautify URLs pretty_urls.trailing_index Whether to keep trailing index.html in permalinks; removed when set to false true pretty_urls.trailing_html Whether to keep trailing .html in permalinks; removed when set to false (no effect on trailing index.html) true

# Directory source_dir: source public_dir: public tag_dir: tags archive_dir: archives category_dir: categories code_dir: downloads/code i18n_dir: :lang skip_render: Setting Description Default source_dir Source folder where your content is stored source public_dir Public folder where generated static files are stored public tag_dir Tag directory tags archive_dir Archive directory archives category_dir Category directory categories code_dir Include code directory downloads/code i18n_dir Internationalization (i18n) directory :lang skip_render Skip rendering for specified files; you can use glob expressions to match paths

# Writing new_post_name: :title.md default_layout: post titlecase: false external_link: enable: true field: site exclude: '' filename_case: 0 render_drafts: false post_asset_folder: false relative_link: false future: true highlight: enable: true line_number: true auto_detect: false tab_replace: '' wrap: true hljs: false prismjs: enable: false preprocess: true line_number: true tab_replace: '' Setting Description Default new_post_name Filename of new posts :title.md default_layout Default layout post auto_spacing Add spaces between Western and East Asian characters false titlecase Transform titles into title case false external_link Open external links in a new tab true external_link.enable Open external links in a new tab true external_link.field Applies to the whole site or post only site external_link.exclude Exclude hostname. Specify subdomain when applicable, including www [] filename_case Transform filenames to: 1 lowercase or 2 uppercase 0 render_drafts Render drafts false post_asset_folder Enable Asset Folder false relative_link Make links relative to the root folder false future Display future posts true highlight Code block settings, see Highlight.js section for usage guide prismjs Code block settings, see PrismJS section for usage guide

# Home page setting # path: Root path for your blogs index page. (default = '') # per_page: Posts displayed per page. (0 = disable pagination) # order_by: Posts order. (Order by date descending by default) index_generator: path: '' per_page: 10 order_by: -date
# Category & Tag default_category: uncategorized category_map: tag_map: Setting Description Default default_category Default category uncategorized category_map Category slugs tag_map Tag slugs

# Date / Time format ## Hexo uses Moment.js to parse and display date ## You can customize the date format as defined in ## http://momentjs.com/docs/#/displaying/format/ date_format: YYYY-MM-DD time_format: HH:mm:ss ## updated_option supports 'mtime', 'date', 'empty' updated_option: 'mtime'
# Pagination per_page: 10 pagination_dir: page Setting Description Default per_page Amount of posts displayed per page (0 = disable pagination) 10 pagination_dir Pagination directory page

# Include / Exclude file(s) ## include:/exclude: options only apply to the 'source/' folder include: exclude: ignore: Setting Description include Hexo ignores hidden files and folders by default, but files listed here will still be processed by Hexo exclude Files listed here will be ignored by Hexo ignore Ignore files/folders

# Extensions ## Plugins: https://hexo.io/plugins/ ## Themes: https://hexo.io/themes/ theme: next # Deployment ## Docs: https://hexo.io/docs/one-command-deployment deploy: type: git repo: https://github.com/Kiwi0093/Kiwi0093.github.io branch: master Setting Description theme Theme name; set to false to disable theming deploy Deployment settings

Due to GitHub's policy changes, logging in with a username/password over HTTPS is no longer supported, so the deploy configuration must be updated to the following: # Deployment ## Docs: https://hexo.io/docs/one-command-deployment deploy: type: git repo: https://<token>@github.com/Kiwi0093/Kiwi0093.github.io branch: master Note that with this setting, hexo d -g no longer prompts for a username/password, but if this token ever leaks it can be a serious security issue. The simplest mitigation is to make the entire repo private to reduce exposure. Updated 2026-11-27 GitHub has completely deprecated HTTPS password authentication, and storing a Personal Access Token in plaintext inside _config.yml (https://<token>@github.com/...) still poses a credential leak risk. Modern practice is to use an SSH deploy key (git@github.com:...), a system credential manager, or GitHub Actions with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN to automatically deploy to GitHub Pages.

Add a categories main page: hexo new page categories Add a tags main page: hexo new page tags Edit source/tags/index.md: --- type: "tags" ---

First, install npm-check-updates: # Manjaro Environment pacman -S npm-check-updates Useful commands: # Check which packages are outdated npm outdated # Check for the latest packages npm-check-updates # Update package.json ncu -u # Update packages npm install Additionally, when git clone is used to fetch the entire blog (including package.json), you do not need to re-run installation commands: # Update the entire node_modules according to package.json npm update Updated 2026-11-27 The historical commands above contain several errors and outdated syntax; they are retained for archival reference: The package name should be npm-check-updates (with a trailing s), and since it is typically not included in official Arch/Manjaro repositories, it should be installed via npm install -g npm-check-updates. The npm subcommand to check for outdated packages is npm outdated (misspelled as npm outdate in the original text). documents.t: The NexT theme is a very beautiful blog theme/style and is very simple to install. You can install it directly using npm.

There are two installation methods on the NexT Theme Official Website: Install directly via npm (requires Hexo version 5.0 or above) # Inside the Hexo directory npm install hexo-theme-next After installation, directly modify the theme section in the Hexo directory's _config.yml to use it: theme: next Clone the entire theme directly into Hexo's theme directory using Git commands Since V8, npm installation is essentially used. # Inside the Hexo directory git clone https://github.com/next-theme/hexo-theme-next themes/next After installation, you still need to modify the Hexo directory's _config.yml: theme: next

Copy the Theme's _config.yml as _config.[Theme_name].yml (e.g., _config.next.yml). For detailed instructions, refer to the Official Documentation. Basically, you only need to modify the following main parameters:

# --------------------------------------------------------------- # Scheme Settings # --------------------------------------------------------------- # Schemes #scheme: Muse scheme: Mist #scheme: Pisces #scheme: Gemini # Dark Mode darkmode: true There are four schemes to choose from, with examples available on the official website: Muse, Mist, Pisces, Gemini. You can choose one and modify the configuration to enable it. Additionally, NexT now natively supports Dark Mode. It is false by default; changing it to true enables dark mode. Manual Toggle for Dark Mode​ References​ Clay's Technical Blog Configuration Method​ Install Plug-in​ $ npm install hexo-next-darkmode --save Configuration​ #_config.next.yml --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- # disable default Darkmode darkmode: false # add below # Darkmode JS # For more information: https://github.com/rqh656418510/hexo-next-darkmode, https://github.com/sandoche/Darkmode.js darkmode_js: enable: true bottom: '64px' # default: '32px' right: 'unset' # default: '32px' left: '32px' # default: 'unset' time: '0.5s' # default: '0.3s' mixColor: 'transparent' # default: '#fff' backgroundColor: 'transparent' # default: '#fff' buttonColorDark: '#100f2c' # default: '#100f2c' buttonColorLight: '#fff' # default: '#fff' isActivated: false # default false saveInCookies: true # default: true label: '🌓' # default: '' autoMatchOsTheme: true # default: true libUrl: # Set custom library cdn url for Darkmode.js isActivated: true: Use Dark Mode by default; recommended to pair with saveInCookies: false, autoMatchOsTheme: false.

# --------------------------------------------------------------- # Menu Settings # --------------------------------------------------------------- menu: home: / || fa fa-home #about: /about/ || fa fa-user tags: /tags/ || fa fa-tags categories: /categories/ || fa fa-th archives: /archives/ || fa fa-archive #schedule: /schedule/ || fa fa-calendar #sitemap: /sitemap.xml || fa fa-sitemap #commonweal: /404/ || fa fa-heartbeat wiki: https://kiwi0093.github.io/Wiki-site/ || fa fa-sitemap # Enable / Disable menu icons / item badges. menu_settings: icons: true badges: false Editing this section can easily create a menu within the blog framework. The official documentation also introduces hierarchical menu syntax, as follows: menu: home: / || fa fa-home archives: /archives/ || fa fa-archive Docs: default: /docs/ || fa fa-book Getting Started: default: /getting-started/ || fa fa-flag Installation: /installation.html || fa fa-download Configuration: /configuration.html || fa fa-wrench Third Party Services: default: /third-party-services/ || fa fa-puzzle-piece Math Equations: /math-equations.html || fa fa-square-root-alt Comment Systems: /comments.html || fa fa-comment-alt For other detailed settings, refer to the official documentation. Under the architecture at that time, it was crucial to include: wiki: https://kiwi0093.github.io/Wiki-site/ || fa fa-sitemap to create the Wiki link.

Otherwise you need a reverse proxy for it. # For example: # api: https://disqus.skk.moe/disqus/ api: apikey: ${Your_API_KEY} # Register new application from https://disqus.com/api/applications/ shortname: ${your_shortname} # See: https://disqus.com/admin/settings/general/ Once done, run hexo clean and hexo d -g

documents.s: Hexo Wikitten Theme Installation and Configuration (Archived)

documents.t: This was the main framework I previously used to set up this Wiki site. Except for some color customizations I made myself, the rest is in its original form.

Installing this theme is relatively simple, with only the git clone installation method: # Inside the Hexo directory git clone https://github.com/zthxxx/hexo-theme-Wikitten.git themes/Wikitten Copy the following files: cp -rf themes/Wikitten/_source/* source/ cp -rf themes/Wikitten/_scaffolds/* scaffolds/ cp -f themes/Wikitten/_config.yml.example _config.Wikitten.yml Install the following plugins: hexo-autonofollow: Automatically open external links in a new tab. hexo-directory-category: Automatically assign categories to posts based on their file directory. hexo-generator-feed: Generate RSS feeds. hexo-generator-json-content: Generate JSON content for full-text search across the site. hexo-generator-sitemap: Generate a site sitemap. npm i -S hexo-autonofollow hexo-directory-category hexo-generator-feed hexo-generator-json-content hexo-generator-sitemap Modify _config.yml: theme: Wikitten

According to the original architectural design, the Wiki was installed separately inside Wiki-site, so part of the Wiki-related settings in _config.yml needed to be modified. Site & URL​ # Site title: Kiwi's Wiki subtitle: description: '' keywords: author: Kiwi language: en timezone: '' # URL ## If your site is put in a subdirectory, set url as 'http://example.com/child' and root as '/child/' url: http://Kiwi0093.github.io/Wiki-site root: /Wiki-site permalink: wiki/:title/ permalink_defaults: pretty_urls: trailing_index: true # Set to false to remove trailing 'index.html' from permalinks trailing_html: true # Set to false to remove trailing '.html' from permalinks Since it is a Wiki-Site, the root part needs to be changed to /Wiki-site, and permalink modified to wiki/:title/. Directories​ # Directory source_dir: source public_dir: public tag_dir: tags archive_dir: archives category_dir: categories code_dir: downloads/code i18n_dir: :lang skip_render: - README.md - '_posts/**/embed_page/**' Add the following under skip_render: - README.md - '_posts/**/embed_page/**' Theme and Deployment​ # Extensions ## Plugins: https://hexo.io/plugins/ ## Themes: https://hexo.io/themes/ theme: Wikitten # Deployment ## Docs: https://hexo.io/docs/one-command-deployment deploy: type: git repo: https://github.com/Kiwi0093/Wiki-site branch: gh-pages For the deploy section, branch needs to be changed to gh-pages to ensure web pages are deployed to https://kiwi0093.github.io/Wiki-site/.

Menu​ # Menus menu: Home: / Archives: /archives Categories: /categories Tags: /tags About: /about Blog : https://Kiwi0093.github.io Remember to add Blog : https://Kiwi0093.github.io to ensure there is a link back to the Blog on the Wiki pages. Customize​ # Customize customize: logo: enabled: true width: 40 height: 40 url: /logo.png profile: enabled: false # Whether to show profile bar avatar: # css/images/avatar.png gravatar: Kiwi@kaienroid.com # Gravatar email address, if you enable Gravatar, your avatar config will be overriden author: Kiwi author_title: Designer & Programmer location: Taipei, Taiwan follow: https://github.com/Kiwi0093/ highlight: monokai sidebar: left # sidebar position, options: left, right category_perExpand: false # enable article categories list per expanding thumbnail: true # enable posts thumbnail, options: true, false favicon: /favicon.ico # path to favicon default_index_file: index.md # if this, it will display at site index instead of default index page social_links: github: https://github.com/Kiwi0093/Kiwi0093.github.io rss: /atom.xml social_link_tooltip: true # enable the social link tooltip, options: true, false This section primarily configures the framework layout. Widgets​ # Widgets widgets: # default use category only - category # - recent_posts # - archive # - tag # - tagcloud # - links This configures which items are listed in the left/right sidebars. Version History Control​ # History version history_control: # make you wiki has history version control in page enable: true server_link: https://github.com # recommend use GitHub https://github.com user: Kiwi0093 repertory: Wiki-site branch: master This allows the Wiki's version history to integrate directly with GitHub version control.

When hosting a Docusaurus-based Wiki / Blog on GitHub Pages, project sites are published by default under a subpath named after the repository (e.g., https://kiwi0093.github.io/Public-Wiki/). To visit the website as a root site under an independent subdomain (such as https://blog.kiwireich.com/), binding a custom domain directly to the GitHub Pages project is the most concise solution. This approach requires no changes to the GitHub repository name (no need to rename it to kiwi0093.github.io) and does not affect the existing homepage, automatically mounting the project at the root path / of the custom domain.
documents.s: GitHub Pages Custom Domain Binding and Docusaurus Root Path Migration Guide

documents.t: Before Migration: https://kiwi0093.github.io/Public-Wiki/ (Project site, assets and routing rely on the /Public-Wiki/ prefix). After Migration: https://blog.kiwireich.com/ (Independent domain site, assets and routing return to the root directory /). Maintenance Benefits: The original repository name Public-Wiki (or Public_wiki) remains unchanged. The existing kiwi0093.github.io repository is undisturbed, avoiding destructive relocation to /old/. Root directory routing is naturally established, resolving cross-platform static asset referencing and hierarchical path misalignment issues.

Log in to the DNS control panel managing your primary domain (kiwireich.com) (such as Cloudflare or your DNS hosting provider), and add a CNAME record for the subdomain: Record Type Name / Host Target / Value TTL Proxy Status (if using Cloudflare) CNAME blog kiwi0093.github.io Auto DNS only (Gray cloud) Tip: If your DNS is hosted on Cloudflare, it is recommended to disable the proxy (turn it into a gray cloud) during initial binding to prevent Cloudflare's edge caching and SSL termination mechanisms from interfering with GitHub's automatic Let's Encrypt certificate issuance.
documents.s: Step A: Configure DNS CNAME Resolution Records

documents.t: Since the domain has changed and the path has shifted from a subdirectory to the root path, you need to calibrate the website's base URL and base path accordingly: Edit docusaurus.config.js (or docusaurus.config.ts) in the root directory of your Wiki project: module.exports = { // Change the site main URL to the specified custom subdomain url: 'https://blog.kiwireich.com', // [Critical Fix]: Changed from original '/Public-Wiki/' to root directory '/' baseUrl: '/', // GitHub Pages deployment related declarations (keep as is) organizationName: 'kiwi0093', projectName: 'Public-Wiki', trailingSlash: false, // ... remaining theme, navbar, and plugin configurations remain unchanged ... }; Updated 2026-11-27 The url field in line 3 of the original example was mistakenly written as Markdown link syntax ('[https://blog.kiwireich.com](https://blog.kiwireich.com)'). Please fill it in with a plain URL string 'https://blog.kiwireich.com', otherwise Docusaurus build will fail due to URL format validation errors: url: 'https://blog.kiwireich.com',

When GitHub Pages binds a custom domain, it writes a file named CNAME to the root of the publishing branch (such as gh-pages). If the project is built by automation tools like GitHub Actions, every build overwrites the publishing branch with ./build, causing the domain configured manually in web settings to be overwritten and cleared. Include CNAME in Docusaurus's static asset directory (static/), and the build process will automatically copy it to the output root directory: Create a file named static/CNAME (note: no file extension) under the project's static/ folder. The content should only contain a single line with your custom domain name: blog.kiwireich.com
documents.s: Step C: Create Static CNAME Declaration File (Prevent CI/CD Overwriting)

documents.t: Commit and push your settings and static files to GitHub: git add docusaurus.config.js static/CNAME git commit -m "feat: configure custom domain blog.kiwireich.com and set baseUrl to root" git push origin main After pushing, check the Actions tab of your GitHub repository to ensure the automated deployment workflow completes successfully.
documents.s: Step D: Push Changes and Trigger GitHub Actions

documents.t: Open the Public-Wiki repository on GitHub. Click Settings ➔ Pages in the left sidebar. Check the Custom domain field: The system should now automatically populate blog.kiwireich.com (if not, enter it manually and click Save). DNS Verification and Certificate Issuance: The system will automatically perform a DNS check. Once passed, GitHub will request a TLS/SSL certificate for the domain (usually takes about 5 to 15 minutes). Once certificate issuance is complete, check Enforce HTTPS to ensure all unencrypted HTTP traffic is automatically redirected to HTTPS.
documents.s: Step E: Confirm in GitHub Repository Settings and Enforce HTTPS

documents.t: Open https://blog.kiwireich.com/ in a browser and verify that the homepage loads normally without layout breakage. Check loading paths of CSS, JS, and image assets, confirming they all start with https://blog.kiwireich.com/assets/... rather than the old /Public-Wiki/ path. Check internal cross-page links in Wiki and Blog to confirm route switching has no 404 errors. Check SSL certificate status to ensure the browser address bar displays a secure encryption padlock indicator.

documents.s: Docusaurus + GitHub Actions Automated Build & GitHub Pages Deployment

documents.t: GitHub Pages currently supports two publishing modes: GitHub Actions Native Artifact Publishing (Recommended): Build artifacts (build/) are directly sent as binary zip packages to the underlying GitHub Pages infrastructure. There is no need to maintain an extra gh-pages branch filled with build noise in the repository, making it clean and extremely fast to execute. Traditional Branch Override Publishing (gh-pages Branch): The Action automatically creates a gh-pages branch and commits static artifacts to it.

During compilation, Docusaurus strictly calculates the absolute paths of all resources (CSS, JS, images) based on url and baseUrl. Incorrect path configurations are the primary cause of broken styles (layout corruption) and 404 errors after deploying to GitHub Pages.
documents.s: 2. Prerequisites: Aligning Repository and docusaurus.config.js URLs

documents.t: Assuming your GitHub account is kiwihome and your repository name is kiwi-wiki: url: https://kiwihome.github.io (or your custom domain if bound, e.g., https://wiki.example.com) baseUrl: /<Repo Name>/ (must have leading and trailing slashes, e.g., /kiwi-wiki/; if using a custom apex domain, this must be changed to `'/') organizationName: GitHub organization or personal account name projectName: Repository name trailingSlash: Explicitly specify whether to include a trailing slash (recommended to set to false to prevent specific anchor link redirection failures on GitHub Pages) Edit docusaurus.config.js in the project root: // @ts-check /** @type {import('@docusaurus/types').Config} */ const config = { title: 'My HomeLab Wiki', tagline: 'Automated Operations & Technical Documentation Library', favicon: 'img/favicon.ico', // Core path declarations (strictly replace according to your project) url: 'https://<USERNAME>.github.io', baseUrl: '/<REPO_NAME>/', organizationName: '<USERNAME>', projectName: '<REPO_NAME>', trailingSlash: false, onBrokenLinks: 'throw', // Abruptly abort build on broken links to prevent dirty data deployment onBrokenMarkdownLinks: 'warn', // ... Remaining theme and plugin configurations remain unchanged }; module.exports = config; Updated 2026-11-27 In Docusaurus 3.9+, the top-level onBrokenMarkdownLinks option has been marked as deprecated. It is recommended to move it to markdown: { hooks: { onBrokenMarkdownLinks: 'warn' } }.

Before pushing the Workflow, you must navigate to the GitHub repository web interface to grant permissions: Open the target GitHub repository. Click Settings in the top navigation bar. Find Pages in the left menu (under the Code and automation section): Build and deployment -> Source: Change the default Deploy from a branch to GitHub Actions. Click Actions -> General in the left menu: Scroll to the Workflow permissions section. Ensure Read and write permissions is selected. Check Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests (if prompted), and click Save.
documents.s: 3. One-Time GitHub Repository Console Permission Settings

documents.t: Create the directory and file in the local project root: .github/workflows/deploy.yml.

This configuration uses GitHub's official upload-pages-artifact and deploy-pages modules, requiring no Personal Access Token (PAT) and relying entirely on the runner's built-in short-lived OIDC Token for secure deployment. name: Deploy Docusaurus to GitHub Pages on: push: branches: - main # Trigger branch; adjust if your default is master # Strictly define Workflow permissions permissions: contents: read # Read repository code pages: write # Write GitHub Pages artifact id-token: write # Used for OIDC authentication to achieve keyless deployment # Avoid concurrency conflicts when multiple commits are pushed simultaneously; automatically cancel the previous unfinished task concurrency: group: 'pages' cancel-in-progress: false jobs: build: name: Build Docusaurus runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - name: Checkout repository uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: # fetch-depth: 0 means fetching the full Git history # Crucial: If set to 1, Docusaurus will not be able to retrieve document "last edited time" and "author information" fetch-depth: 0 - name: Setup Node.js uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: 20 cache: npm # Automatically cache ~/.npm directory to significantly speed up npm ci time - name: Install dependencies # Use npm ci instead of npm install to strictly restore versions based on package-lock.json run: npm ci - name: Build website # Compile and generate the static build/ directory run: npm run build - name: Upload Pages artifact uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3 with: path: build/ # Specify Docusaurus compilation output directory deploy: name: Deploy to GitHub Pages needs: build runs-on: ubuntu-latest environment: name: github-pages url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }} steps: - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages id: deployment uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4 Updated 2026-11-27 The comment "automatically cancel the previous unfinished task" in the YAML above is opposite to the actual setting cancel-in-progress: false: setting it to false allows ongoing deployment tasks to finish and queue up (which is GitHub's official recommendation for Pages deployments to prevent interruptions mid-deployment). node-version: 20: Node.js 20 reached End-of-Life (EOL) on 2026-04-30; it is recommended to upgrade to a current LTS version (such as 22 or 24).
documents.s: Option A: Modern Native Pages Deployment (Strongly Recommended, Zero Branch Pollution)

documents.t: If your organization's project guidelines require physical files and commit history to be visible in the branch list, you can use Docusaurus's official built-in CLI publishing script: name: Deploy to gh-pages Branch on: push: branches: - main permissions: contents: write # Must have write permission to the repository to create branches jobs: deploy: name: Deploy via Docusaurus CLI runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - name: Checkout uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: fetch-depth: 0 - name: Setup Node.js uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: 20 cache: npm - name: Install dependencies run: npm ci - name: Deploy to gh-pages run: | git config --global user.name "github-actions[bot]" git config --global user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com" npx docusaurus deploy env: # Use built-in GITHUB_TOKEN, no manual Secret configuration needed GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} Updated 2026-11-27 node-version: 20: Node.js 20 reached End-of-Life (EOL) on 2026-04-30; it is recommended to upgrade to a current LTS version (such as 22 or 24).
documents.s: Option B: Traditional Push to gh-pages Branch (Compatible with Legacy Architecture)

documents.t: If you plan to bind your own domain to the Wiki (e.g., wiki.example.com):

Create a plain text file named CNAME (without file extension) under the static/ directory of your project, and fill it with your domain name: wiki.example.com Files placed under static/ are automatically copied verbatim to the build/ root during build.
documents.s: Step 1: Create a CNAME Static File

documents.t: url: 'https://wiki.example.com', baseUrl: '/', // After binding a custom domain, baseUrl must be changed back to the root path '/'

Add a CNAME record at your DNS provider: Name: wiki Target: <USERNAME>.github.io Proxy status: If using Cloudflare, it is recommended to set it to DNS Only (Grey Cloud) when first applying for the certificate, and evaluate enabling the Orange Cloud after GitHub successfully issues the Let's Encrypt certificate and enables "Enforce HTTPS".
documents.s: Step 3: DNS Settings (Using Cloudflare / DNS Provider as an Example)

documents.t: Cause: Docusaurus has built-in fool-proofing mechanisms during compilation. If Markdown text references non-existent document file names, has incorrect relative paths, or references non-existent Markdown anchors (#section-title), the build will be forcibly aborted. Resolution: Inspect the Action execution logs; the output will clearly indicate which file and line number contains the broken link. Fix the path; if a specific page is still in draft stage, add draft: true to that Markdown's Frontmatter to skip compilation.
documents.s: 6.1 Action Build Fails with Docusaurus found broken links! in Logs

documents.t: Cause: baseUrl does not match the GitHub repository name. For example, if the repository is named my-wiki, but baseUrl was set to '/', causing the browser to fetch resources from https://<User>.github.io/assets/css/... instead of https://<User>.github.io/my-wiki/assets/css/.... Resolution: Review docusaurus.config.js and ensure baseUrl: '/<REPO_NAME>/' has slashes at both ends.
documents.s: 6.2 Visiting the Website After Deployment Shows a Blank Page with Numerous 404 Errors in Console

documents.t: Cause: Actions write permissions are not enabled for the repository. Resolution: Go to repository Settings -> Actions -> General -> Workflow permissions, switch to Read and write permissions, and click Save.
documents.s: 6.3 Action Reports Permission to ... denied to github-actions[bot]

documents.t: Cause: When the document count reaches hundreds or more, Node.js default heap memory (around 1.5GB) is exhausted while compiling Webpack artifacts. Resolution: Inject Node environment variables before the build step in the Workflow to increase the memory limit: - name: Build website run: npm run build env: NODE_OPTIONS: "--max-old-space-size=4096"
documents.s: 6.4 npm start Runs Locally, but npm run build Throws Out-Of-Memory (OOM) in Actions

documents.t: A standard Docusaurus site consists of documentation (docs), a blog (blog), and custom React pages (src/pages): my-website/ ├── docs/ <-- Markdown / MDX technical docs (sidebar tree structure) │ ├── intro.md │ └── tutorial/ ├── blog/ <-- Timeline articles (Blog mode, optional to disable) ├── static/ <-- Static assets (images, favicon, robots.txt) ├── src/ │ ├── css/custom.css <-- Custom styles (supports overriding dark/light variables) │ └── pages/index.js <-- Landing page ├── docusaurus.config.js <-- Core global config (site name, routes, plugins) ├── sidebars.js <-- Sidebar structure definition └── package.json <-- Dependency management and startup scripts
It is recommended to use the officially recommended classic template: # Create project using Node.js 18+ npx create-docusaurus@latest my-website classic cd my-website

# Start local live preview server (default Port: 3000, supports HMR hot reload) npm start # Build static artifacts (output to build/ directory for production release) npm run build # Locally preview the built static files npm run serve

The configuration file is responsible for defining the site's base URL, Navbar, Footer, and default plugins: // @ts-check const {themes} = require('prism-react-renderer'); /** @type {import('@docusaurus/types').Config} */ const config = { title: 'My HomeLab Wiki', tagline: 'Automation Ops & Self-Hosted Services Technical Manual', favicon: 'img/favicon.ico', // Production URL settings url: 'https://wiki.example.com', baseUrl: '/', // Used for GitHub Pages deployment (can be anything if not using GH Pages) organizationName: 'my-org', projectName: 'my-wiki', onBrokenLinks: 'throw', // Abort build on broken links (CI/CD safeguard) onBrokenMarkdownLinks: 'warn', i18n: { defaultLocale: 'zh-Hant', // Default locale: Traditional Chinese locales: ['zh-Hant', 'en'], }, presets: [ [ 'classic', /** @type {import('@docusaurus/preset-classic').Options} */ ({ docs: { sidebarPath: './sidebars.js', routeBasePath: 'docs', // Docs root path; if set to '/', the entire site acts solely as a doc site editUrl: undefined, // Disable "Edit this page" button (applicable to private repos) }, blog: false, // If acting purely as a Wiki knowledge base, can be set to false to close blog theme: { customCss: './src/css/custom.css', }, }), ], ], themeConfig: /** @type {import('@docusaurus/preset-classic').ThemeConfig} */ ({ navbar: { title: 'HomeLab Wiki', logo: { alt: 'Site Logo', src: 'img/logo.svg', }, items: [ { type: 'docSidebar', sidebarId: 'tutorialSidebar', position: 'left', label: 'Documentation', }, { href: 'https://github.com/my-org/my-wiki', label: 'GitHub', position: 'right', }, ], }, colorMode: { defaultMode: 'dark', // Default to dark mode respectPrefersColorScheme: true, }, prism: { theme: themes.github, darkTheme: themes.dracula, additionalLanguages: ['bash', 'yaml', 'docker', 'nginx', 'json'], // Extended syntax highlighting }, }), }; module.exports = config; Updated 2026-11-27 Starting from Docusaurus v3.9, the top-level configuration onBrokenMarkdownLinks has been deprecated (scheduled for removal in v4). It is recommended to migrate it under markdown.hooks.onBrokenMarkdownLinks: markdown: { hooks: { onBrokenMarkdownLinks: 'warn', }, },

Sidebars are divided into "Auto-generated" and "Manual" modes. For a Wiki with a large volume of documents, the auto-generated mode is strongly recommended, utilizing the directory structure and Markdown Frontmatter to control sorting.

// @ts-check /** @type {import('@docusaurus/plugin-content-docs').SidebarsConfig} */ const sidebars = { tutorialSidebar: [ { type: 'autogenerated', dirName: '.', // Automatically recursively scan all folders and files under docs/ }, ], }; module.exports = sidebars;

Adding YAML metadata at the top of each Markdown file allows precise control over its name and weight in the sidebar: --- id: uptime-kuma-guide title: Uptime Kuma Monitoring Manual sidebar_label: Uptime Kuma Monitoring # Short name displayed in sidebar sidebar_position: 1 # Sorting weight (smaller numbers appear higher) description: Cross-host container guarding and status page setup tags: - Docker - Monitoring --- # Uptime Kuma Monitoring Manual Body...

To set a sidebar display name for a subfolder inside docs/, place a _category_.json inside that folder: { "label": "Media Streaming Packages", "position": 2, "link": { "type": "generated-index", "description": "Covers integration guides for Navidrome, Emby, and Lidarr." } }
Docusaurus supports direct use of special warning boxes (Admonitions) and React UI components within Markdown:

:::tip[Practical Tip] When mounting a music library via NFS, adding the `_netdev` option prevents boot hangs. ::: :::warning[Precautions] Do not store SQLite databases on CIFS/SMB network shares. ::: :::danger[Severe Warning] Be sure to perform snapshot backups before executing data cleanups! :::

Suitable for demonstrating comparative commands across different operating systems or tools: import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs'; import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem'; <Tabs> <TabItem value="photon" label="Photon OS" default> ```bash tdnf -y install cifs-utils ``` </TabItem> <TabItem value="debian" label="Debian / Ubuntu"> ```bash apt-get update && apt-get install -y cifs-utils ``` </TabItem> </Tabs>

Docusaurus officially recommends Algolia by default, but when building an internal private knowledge base, external crawlers cannot access it. The community's most mature offline solution is @easyops-cn/docusaurus-search-local.
documents.s: 6. Local Full-Text Search Engine Integration (Zero External Dependencies)

documents.t: npm install @easyops-cn/docusaurus-search-local

// Add the themes block within the config object: themes: [ [ require.resolve('@easyops-cn/docusaurus-search-local'), /** @type {import("@easyops-cn/docusaurus-search-local").PluginOptions} */ ({ hashed: true, language: ['zh', 'en'], // Supports Chinese and English word segmentation search indexDocs: true, indexBlog: false, docsRouteBasePath: '/docs', }), ], ], Once configured, running npm run build will automatically build index files locally, and an offline search bar will appear directly at the top of the site.
Docusaurus compiled outputs consist purely of static files (located in the build/ directory). Common self-hosted containerization modes involve Docker Nginx containers or pairing with Traefik v3.

Create a Dockerfile utilizing a Node container for compilation and an Alpine Nginx image for serving, resulting in a size of around 20MB: # Stage 1: Build FROM node:20-alpine AS builder WORKDIR /app COPY package*.json ./ RUN npm ci COPY . . RUN npm run build # Stage 2: Serve FROM nginx:alpine COPY --from=builder /app/build /usr/share/nginx/html COPY nginx.conf /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf EXPOSE 80 CMD ["nginx", "-g", "daemon off;"] Updated 2026-11-27 Node.js 20 (associated with node:20-alpine) reached its official End-of-Life (EOL) on 2026-04-30. It is recommended to update the build stage base image to a currently maintained LTS version (such as node:22-alpine or node:24-alpine). Corresponding nginx.conf: server { listen 80; server_name localhost; root /usr/share/nginx/html; index index.html; location / { try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html; } # Enable Gzip compression for static assets gzip on; gzip_types text/plain text/css application/json application/javascript text/xml application/xml image/svg+xml; }

services: wiki: build: . container_name: docusaurus-wiki restart: unless-stopped networks: - proxy-network labels: - "traefik.enable=true" - "traefik.http.routers.wiki.rule=Host(`wiki.example.com`)" - "traefik.http.routers.wiki.entrypoints=websecure" - "traefik.http.routers.wiki.tls=true" - "traefik.http.routers.wiki.tls.certresolver=myresolver" - "traefik.http.services.wiki.loadbalancer.server.port=80" networks: proxy-network: external: true

documents.t: Anomaly Root Cause Resolution npm run build throws Docusaurus found broken links! Cross-page hyperlink paths in the text are incorrect, or referenced anchors do not exist. Fix paths according to the file line numbers printed in logs, or temporarily change onBrokenLinks to 'warn' in docusaurus.config.js. Markdown contains special characters causing build failure The MDX parser misinterprets < or { as JSX tags or code variables. Wrap inline code in backticks (e.g., `<Your_IP>`) or replace with HTML entity encoding. Chinese strings cannot be searched The search plugin lacks Chinese word segmentation support. Verify that @easyops-cn/docusaurus-search-local configuration includes language: ["zh", "en"]. Custom styles breaking in dark mode CSS hardcodes color codes without overriding global CSS variables. Edit src/css/custom.css and override theme variables like --ifm-color-primary inside the [data-theme='dark'] selector.

documents.t: Primary Choice: v2rayNG (Intuitive interface, most complete Xray core support, full support for Reality/Vision features) Advanced Alternative: sing-box (Android Official Version) (Powerful rule-based routing, extremely low battery consumption)

Fastest Import Method (Clipboard Import)​ Copy the vless:// link of the node in the 3X-UI panel. Open v2rayNG, tap the + icon in the upper right corner -> Select "Import config from clipboard". Tap the V icon in the lower right corner to connect, and tap the status bar below to test latency. Manual Setup for VLESS-Reality​ Tap + in the upper right corner -> "Manually input [VLESS]". Fill in the fields sequentially: Remark: Reality-Direct Address: reality.yourdomain.com Port: 443 UUID (id): Enter your UUID Flow (flow): Select xtls-rprx-vision Network (network): tcp Stream Security (streamSecurity): Select reality SNI: reality.yourdomain.com Fingerprint (uTLS): chrome PublicKey: Enter the Public Key generated by 3X-UI ShortId: Enter the corresponding Short ID Tap the checkmark in the upper right corner to save. Manual Setup for VLESS-WS+TLS+CDN​ Tap + in the upper right corner -> "Manually input [VLESS]". Fill in the fields sequentially: Remark: WS-CDN-Rescue Address: cdn.yourdomain.com (or Cloudflare Preferred IP) Port: 443 UUID (id): Enter your UUID Flow (flow): Leave blank Network (network): Select ws WebSocket -> path: /ray-ws-stream WebSocket -> host: cdn.yourdomain.com Stream Security (streamSecurity): Select tls SNI: cdn.yourdomain.com Tap the checkmark in the upper right corner to save.
Primary Choice: Shadowrocket (Best cost-performance ratio, one-time purchase, great compatibility, supports Reality and uTLS) Alternative / Advanced: Loon, Sing-box, or Stash (Clash for iOS)

Fastest Import Method (QR Code / Link)​ Tap the QR Code icon of the node in the 3X-UI panel. Open Shadowrocket, tap the scan button in the upper left corner to aim at the screen, or copy the vless:// link and open the App for automatic prompt addition. Manual Setup for VLESS-Reality​ Tap + in the upper right corner. Type: Select VLESS. Fill in the fields sequentially: Server: reality.yourdomain.com Port: 443 Password (UUID): Enter UUID Security (Security): Select Reality PublicKey: Enter Public Key Short ID: Enter Short ID Peer (SNI): reality.yourdomain.com Flow (Flow): Select xtls-rprx-vision Fingerprint: Select chrome Tap Save in the upper right corner. Manual Setup for VLESS-WS+TLS+CDN​ Tap + in the upper right corner. Type: Select VLESS. Fill in the fields sequentially: Server: cdn.yourdomain.com Port: 443 Password (UUID): Enter UUID Transport (Transport): Select websocket Path: /ray-ws-stream Host: cdn.yourdomain.com TLS: Enable toggle SNI: cdn.yourdomain.com Tap Save in the upper right corner.

Primary Choice (Intuitive GUI): v2rayN (Supports Xray core, out-of-the-box support for Reality) Primary Choice (Rule-Based Routing): Clash Verge Rev (Based on Mihomo / Clash Meta core, gorgeous UI, supports subscriptions and custom rules)

Quick Import​ Copy the vless:// node text and press Ctrl + V in the main v2rayN window to automatically add it. Manual Addition of VLESS-Reality​ Click Servers at the top -> Add VLESS Server. Align parameters: Address: reality.yourdomain.com Port: 443 UUID (id): Your UUID Flow (flow): xtls-rprx-vision Network (network): tcp Stream Security (streamSecurity): Select reality SNI: reality.yourdomain.com uTLS: chrome PublicKey: Paste Public Key ShortId: Paste Short ID Click OK. Right-click the system tray icon in the lower right corner, and switch "System Proxy" to Set System Proxy (PAC/Global).

Manually add the following proxies snippet into your configuration file: proxies: # 1. Reality Direct Node - name: "Reality-Direct" type: vless server: reality.yourdomain.com port: 443 uuid: YOUR_UUID_HERE network: tcp flow: xtls-rprx-vision tls: true udp: true servername: reality.yourdomain.com client-fingerprint: chrome reality-opts: public-key: YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY_HERE short-id: YOUR_SHORT_ID_HERE # 2. WS+TLS+CDN Rescue Node - name: "CDN-Rescue" type: vless server: cdn.yourdomain.com # Can be replaced with a Cloudflare Preferred IP if blocked port: 443 uuid: YOUR_UUID_HERE cipher: auto tls: true udp: true servername: cdn.yourdomain.com # SNI retains domain name network: ws ws-opts: path: "/ray-ws-stream" headers: Host: cdn.yourdomain.com Updated 2026-11-27 The cipher: auto parameter in the second VLESS node example is a VMess protocol parameter; VLESS itself does not require specifying cipher (the Mihomo core usually ignores it, but it is recommended to omit it in VLESS settings).
documents.s: Option B: Clash Verge Rev (Mihomo Core)

documents.t: Desktop Environment (GUI): Clash Verge Rev (AppImage / .deb / .rpm) Server / Command Line (CLI Primary): sing-box (Single binary executable or Systemd service)

Step 1: Install sing-box​ # Download official binary (using amd64 as an example) bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://sing-box.app/deb-install.sh)" 2>/dev/null || \ curl -Lo /usr/local/bin/sing-box https://github.com/SagerNet/sing-box/releases/latest/download/sing-box-linux-amd64.tar.gz chmod +x /usr/local/bin/sing-box Updated 2026-11-27 The original backup download command contained two errors: GitHub Releases tarballs for SagerNet/sing-box all include version numbers (e.g., sing-box-<VERSION>-linux-amd64.tar.gz), so requesting sing-box-linux-amd64.tar.gz directly results in a 404. Furthermore, .tar.gz files must first be extracted using tar -xzf to obtain the sing-box binary executable before moving it to /usr/local/bin/. For Debian/Ubuntu, it is recommended to use the official deb-install.sh or the official APT repository for installation. Step 2: Configure /etc/sing-box/config.json​ Create the configuration file, locally opening SOCKS5 (Port 10808) and HTTP proxy (Port 10809) (Updated 2026-11-27: The configuration below actually uses a single mixed inbound, providing both HTTP and SOCKS5 proxies simultaneously on Port 10809, and does not enable 10808): { "log": { "level": "info", "timestamp": true }, "inbounds": [ { "type": "mixed", "tag": "mixed-in", "listen": "127.0.0.1", "listen_port": 10809 } ], "outbounds": [ { "type": "vless", "tag": "reality-out", "server": "reality.yourdomain.com", "server_port": 443, "uuid": "YOUR_UUID_HERE", "flow": "xtls-rprx-vision", "network": "tcp", "tls": { "enabled": true, "server_name": "reality.yourdomain.com", "utls": { "enabled": true, "fingerprint": "chrome" }, "reality": { "enabled": true, "public_key": "YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY_HERE", "short_id": "YOUR_SHORT_ID_HERE" } } }, { "type": "vless", "tag": "cdn-out", "server": "cdn.yourdomain.com", "server_port": 443, "uuid": "YOUR_UUID_HERE", "network": "ws", "tls": { "enabled": true, "server_name": "cdn.yourdomain.com" }, "transport": { "type": "ws", "path": "/ray-ws-stream", "headers": { "Host": "cdn.yourdomain.com" } } } ], "route": { "rules": [ { "outbound": "reality-out" } ] } } Updated 2026-11-27 In sing-box version 1.11+, routing rules officially adopt the explicit "action": "route" syntax. If you only need to set a default outbound, it is recommended to write "route" as "rules": [], "final": "reality-out", replacing the unconditional empty rule object. Step 3: Start and Run in Background​ # Test configuration file validity sing-box check -c /etc/sing-box/config.json # Start running directly sing-box run -c /etc/sing-box/config.json # Test connection curl -x http://127.0.0.1:10809 https://ip.sb

documents.s: 3X-UI + Traefik v3 Three Independent Domains Single Port 443 Multiplexing Deployment

documents.t: Independent Domain Plan External Port Traefik Routing Tier TLS Certificate Handler 3X-UI Internal Listen Port Internal Protocol CDN Proxy Status panel.yourdomain.com 443 Layer 7 HTTP Traefik (Let's Encrypt) 2053 Plain HTTP Grey Cloud (DNS Only) or Orange Cloud reality.yourdomain.com 443 Layer 4 TCP No Decryption Passthrough (Xray handles it) 44300 VLESS-Reality Strict Grey Cloud (DNS Only) cdn.yourdomain.com 443 Layer 7 HTTP/WS Traefik (Let's Encrypt) 44301 Plain WebSocket (Cleartext) Orange Cloud Enabled (Proxied)

Add three A records pointing to the VPS public IP in your domain registrar (using Cloudflare as an example): panel.yourdomain.com A <VPS_IP> DNS Only (or Proxied with Full SSL) reality.yourdomain.com A <VPS_IP> DNS Only (Must disable orange cloud, otherwise TCP native handshake breaks) cdn.yourdomain.com A <VPS_IP> Proxied (Enable orange cloud to hide real IP)
documents.s: 2. DNS Resolution and Critical Cloudflare Configuration

documents.t: SSL/TLS Mode: Switch to Full or Full (Strict) (prevents Cloudflare from returning 520/521 errors when connecting to Traefik port 443). Network: Ensure WebSockets is enabled.

Configure in /opt/3x-ui/docker-compose.yml, attaching 3X-ui to the external bridge network proxy-network where Traefik resides: services: 3x-ui: image: ghcr.io/mhsanaei/3x-ui:latest container_name: 3x-ui restart: unless-stopped environment: - XRAY_VMESS_AEAD_FORCED=false volumes: - /opt/3x-ui/db:/etc/x-ui - /opt/3x-ui/cert:/root/cert networks: - proxy-network labels: - "traefik.enable=true" # ========================================================================= # 1. 3X-UI Web Panel (Independent domain panel.yourdomain.com -> Internal 2053) # ========================================================================= - "traefik.http.routers.xui-panel.rule=Host(`panel.yourdomain.com`)" - "traefik.http.routers.xui-panel.entrypoints=websecure" - "traefik.http.routers.xui-panel.tls=true" - "traefik.http.routers.xui-panel.tls.certresolver=myresolver" - "traefik.http.services.xui-panel.loadbalancer.server.port=2053" # ========================================================================= # 2. VLESS-Reality Direct Connection (Independent domain reality.yourdomain.com -> Internal 44300) # ========================================================================= # Key: HostSNI matches connection name; passthrough=true prevents Traefik from decrypting - "traefik.tcp.routers.xui-reality.rule=HostSNI(`reality.yourdomain.com`)" - "traefik.tcp.routers.xui-reality.entrypoints=websecure" - "traefik.tcp.routers.xui-reality.tls.passthrough=true" - "traefik.tcp.services.xui-reality.loadbalancer.server.port=44300" # ========================================================================= # 3. VLESS-WS + CDN Rescue (Independent domain cdn.yourdomain.com -> Internal 44301) # ========================================================================= # Traefik handles TLS termination, forwarding cleartext WebSocket traffic to Xray - "traefik.http.routers.xui-ws.rule=Host(`cdn.yourdomain.com`)" - "traefik.http.routers.xui-ws.entrypoints=websecure" - "traefik.http.routers.xui-ws.tls=true" - "traefik.http.routers.xui-ws.tls.certresolver=myresolver" - "traefik.http.services.xui-ws.loadbalancer.server.port=44301" networks: proxy-network: external: true Start the container: docker compose -f /opt/3x-ui/docker-compose.yml up -d
Open https://panel.yourdomain.com in a browser to log in to the panel, navigate to Inbounds, and add two nodes:

Remark: Reality-Direct-44300 Protocol: vless Listening IP: 0.0.0.0 Port: 44300 (Matches the port declared in the Compose TCP service) Flow: xtls-rprx-vision Security: Reality uTLS: chrome Dest: reality.yourdomain.com:443 (or swdist.apple.com:443) (Updated 2026-11-27: The Reality Dest / newer 3X-UI Target must not point to reality.yourdomain.com:443 which routes back to the local 44300 port via the same HostSNI, otherwise unvalidated probe connections will form a loop; point it to an external real website supporting TLS 1.3 and HTTP/2 such as swdist.apple.com:443, or another local independent virtual host HTTPS port) Server Names (SNI): reality.yourdomain.com (Must match the HostSNI in Traefik Labels exactly) Private Key / Public Key: Click generate and record the public key Short IDs: Click generate

Remark: WS-CDN-Rescue-44301 Protocol: vless Listening IP: 0.0.0.0 Port: 44301 (Matches the port declared in the Compose HTTP service) Network: ws Path: /ray-ws-stream Security: none (Key: Traefik boundary has already performed TLS certificate decryption; enabling TLS inside the container is strictly prohibited)
Regardless of whether the internal listening port is 44300 or 44301, the server port filled in by external clients is always standard 443.

vless://<UUID>@reality.yourdomain.com:443?type=tcp&security=reality&pbk=<PUBLIC_KEY>&fp=chrome&sni=reality.yourdomain.com&sid=<SHORT_ID>&flow=xtls-rprx-vision#Reality-Direct Address: reality.yourdomain.com Port: 443 Security: reality SNI: reality.yourdomain.com Flow: xtls-rprx-vision

vless://<UUID>@cdn.yourdomain.com:443?type=ws&security=tls&sni=cdn.yourdomain.com&path=%2Fray-ws-stream#CDN-Rescue Address: cdn.yourdomain.com (Can be replaced with Cloudflare preferred IPs if blocked) Port: 443 Security: tls SNI / Host: cdn.yourdomain.com Path: /ray-ws-stream

Reality Handshake Timeout: Check if Cloudflare mistakenly enabled the orange cloud for reality.yourdomain.com; this domain must remain grey cloud (DNS Only). Verify that the SNI entered on the client matches the HostSNI in the Traefik Label exactly. WS Node Throws 502 Bad Gateway: Check whether the Security setting for the 3X-UI backend port 44301 inbound was mistakenly set to tls. Since the outer layer already has Traefik terminating certificates, the container side must be set to none. Panel Fails to Login: Check Traefik's ACME certificate application status and confirm that panel.yourdomain.com has successfully issued a Let's Encrypt certificate.
